body.text: Vādanyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vādanyāya</s> (Logic of Debate)

body.text: nigrahasthānalakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: Definition of <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (grounds for defeat)

body.text: 1. nyāyavādinamapi vādeṣu asadvyavasthopanyāsaiḥ śaṭhā nigṛhṇanti, tanniṣedhārthamidamārabhyate /
body.translated_text: 1. Even those who argue according to proper reasoning are defeated in debates by deceitful opponents through the presentation of invalid rules; this [treatise] is undertaken to prevent that.

children.translated_text: Not stating a member of the proof, and not demonstrating a fault in both [parties],
are <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (grounds for defeat); anything else is not accepted as proper.

body.text: iṣṭasyārthasya siddhiḥ sādhanam. tasya nirvartakam aṅgam. tasya avacanaṃ tasyāṅgasyānuccāraṇaṃ vādino nigrahādhikaraṇam: tadabhyupagamya apratibhayā tūṣṇīmbhāvāt / sādhanāṅgasyāsamarthanād vā //
body.translated_text: <s>Sādhana</s> (proof) is the establishment of the desired object. Its member (<s>aṅga</s>) is that which accomplishes it. The non-statement of that, i.e., the non-utterance of that member of proof, is the ground for the defeat of the debater — because upon accepting that [obligation], one falls silent due to lack of a response; or because one fails to justify a member of the proof.

body.text: 2. [svabhāvahetau sādhanāṅgasamarthanam]
body.translated_text: 2. [Justification of a proof-member in the case of a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential-nature reason)]

body.text: trividhameva hi liṅgamapratyakṣasya siddheraṅgam - svabhāvaḥ, kāryam, anupalambhaśca /
body.translated_text: For indeed, the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that serves as a member for establishing what is not directly perceived is only of three kinds — essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), effect (<s>kārya</s>), and non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>).

body.text: tasya samarthanaṃ sādhyena vyāptiṃ prasādhya dharmiṇi bhāvasādhanam / yathā 'yat sat kṛtakaṃ vā, tat sarvamanityam, yathā ghaṭādiḥ, san kṛtako vā śabdaḥ'; iti /
body.translated_text: The justification of that [inferential mark] is: having established the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), demonstrating its presence in the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor). For example: 'Whatever exists or is produced is entirely impermanent, like a pot and so forth; sound exists or is produced.'

body.text: 3. atrāpi na kaścit kramaniyamaḥ, iṣṭārthasiddherubhayatrāviśeṣāt /
body.translated_text: 3. Here too there is no fixed order [of presentation], since there is no difference in either case for establishing the desired object.

body.text: yasmād dharmiṇi prāk sattvaṃ prasādhya paścādapi vyāptiḥ prasādhyata eva / yathā - ''san śabdaḥ kṛtako vā, yaścaivaṃ sa sarvo 'nityaḥ, yathā - ghaṭādiḥ'; iti /
body.translated_text: Because even if one first establishes the existence [of the reason] in the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor), the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) must still be established afterwards. For example: 'Sound exists or is produced; whatever is such is entirely impermanent, like a pot and so forth.'

body.text: 4. atra vyāptisādhanaṃ viparyaye bādhakapramāṇopadarśanam /
body.translated_text: 4. Here the establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) consists in showing a <s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s> (invalidating cognition) for the contrary case.

body.text: yadi na sarvaṃ sat kṛtakaṃ vā pratikṣaṇavināśi syād, akṣaṇikasya kramayaugapadyābhyāmarthakriyāyogād arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇamato vyāvṛttam - ityasadeva syāt /
body.translated_text: If not everything that exists or is produced were momentarily perishing, then since something non-momentary would be incapable of causal efficacy through either succession or simultaneity, it would be excluded from what is characterized by the capacity for causal efficacy — and thus would be non-existent.

body.text: sarvasāmarthyopākhyāvirahalakṣaṇaṃ hi nirupākhyamiti /
body.translated_text: For that which is devoid of all capacity is without any real nature — this is what 'non-existent' means.

body.text: evaṃ sādhanasya sādhyaviparyaye bādhakapramāṇānupadarśane virodhābhāvādasya viparyayavṛtteradarśane san kṛtako vā syāt, nityaśca ityanivṛttireva śaṅkāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, when no <s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s> (invalidating cognition) is shown for the contrary of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) with respect to the proof, due to the absence of contradiction and the non-observation of its occurrence in the contrary case, the doubt would remain unresolved that [something] might exist or be produced and yet be permanent.

body.text: 5. na ca sarvānupalabdhirbhāvasya bādhikā, tatra sāmarthyaṃ kramākramayogena vyāptaṃ siddham; prakārāntarābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: 5. Nor is the mere non-apprehension of everything an invalidator of existence, for the capacity [for causal efficacy] is established as pervaded by [being exercised through] succession and simultaneity, since there is no other mode.

body.text: tena vyāpakadharmānupalabdhirakṣaṇike sāmarthyaṃ bādhate /
body.translated_text: Therefore, non-apprehension of the pervading property (<s>vyāpakadharmānupalabdhi</s>) invalidates the capacity [for causal efficacy] in what is non-momentary.

body.text: kramayaugapadyāyogasya sāmarthyābhāvena vyāptisiddhernānavasthāprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Since the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is established by the impossibility of [exercising] capacity without succession or simultaneity, there is no fault of infinite regress.

body.text: 6. atrāpyadarśanamapramāṇam, yataḥkramayaugapdyāyogasyaivāsāmarthyena vyāptyasiddheḥ pūrvakasyāpi hetoravyāptiḥ / ihāpi punaḥ sādhanopagame 'navasthāprasaṅga iti cet / na; abhāvasādhanasyādarśanasyāpratiṣedhāt /
body.translated_text: 6. Here too, non-observation is not a [valid] means of cognition, because if the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is not established due to the impossibility of succession and simultaneity being equivalent to the absence of capacity, the prior reason too lacks pervasion. If [one objects that] accepting a further proof here [leads to] an infinite regress — no; because non-observation, which proves absence, is not rejected.

body.text: yadadarśanaṃ viparyayaṃ sādhayati hetoḥ sādhyaviparyaye, tadasya viruddhapratyupasthānād bādhakaṃ pramāṇamucyate /
body.translated_text: That non-observation which establishes the contrary of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) when [the reason occurs] in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — that is called a <s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s> (invalidating cognition) because it brings to mind what is contradictory to [the reason].

body.text: evaṃ hi sa hetuḥ sādhyābhāve 'san sidhyet, yadi tatra pramāṇavatā svaviruddhena bādhyeta / anyathā tatrāsya bādhakāsiddhau saṃśayo durnivāraḥ /
body.translated_text: For thus the <s>hetu</s> (reason), were it to occur in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), would be invalidated by something contradictory to it that possesses epistemic warrant. Otherwise, if no invalidator is established there, the doubt is irremovable.

body.text: tato vyatirekasya sandehādanaikāntikaḥ syāddhetvābhāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, due to the doubt regarding the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), [the reason] would be a pseudo-reason of the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) type.

body.text: nāpyadarśanamātrād vyāvṛttiḥ; viprakṛṣṭeṣvasarvadarśino 'darśanasyābhāvāsādhanād, arvāgdarśanena satāmapi keṣāñcidarthānāmadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there exclusion [of the reason from the contrary] merely from non-observation; because for one who does not perceive everything, non-observation of remote [objects] does not prove their absence, and because even among existing things some objects are not observed due to limited perception.

body.text: 7. bādhakaṃ punaḥ pramāṇam / yatra kramayaugapadyāyogo na tasya kvacit sāmarthyam / asti cākṣaṇike sa iti pravartamānamasāmarthyamasallakṣaṇamākarṣati / teha 'yat sat kṛtakaṃ vā tadanityameva'; iti sidhyati /
body.translated_text: 7. Rather, the <s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s> (invalidating cognition) [is as follows]: Where there is impossibility of succession and simultaneity, there is no capacity whatsoever. And in what is non-momentary, that [impossibility] exists. Thus the operative [argument], attracting [the consequence of] absence of capacity — which is the defining mark of non-existence — [demonstrates that]: 'Whatever exists or is produced is necessarily impermanent.' This is thereby established.

body.text: tāvatā sādhanadharmamātrānvayaḥ sādhyadharmasya svabhāvahetulakṣaṇaṃ ca siddhaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: By that much, the co-presence (<s>anvaya</s>) of the mere proving property with the proved property is established, and the defining mark of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential-nature reason) is also established.

body.text: evaṃ svabhāvahetuprayogeṣu samarthitaṃ sādhanāṅgaṃ bhavati / tasyāsamarthanaṃ sādhanāṅgāvacanam / tad vādinaḥ parājayasthānam; prārabdhārthāsādhanāt / vastutaḥ samarthasya hetorupādāne 'pi sāmarthyāpratipādanāt /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the employment of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential-nature reason), the proof-member is justified. Its non-justification constitutes the non-statement of a proof-member. That is the ground for the defeat of the proponent — because the undertaken purpose is not accomplished; because even when a reason that is actually adequate is presented, its adequacy is not demonstrated.

body.text: 8. [kāryahetau sādhanāṅgasamarthanam]
body.translated_text: 8. [Justification of a proof-member in the case of a <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-reason)]

body.text: kāryahetāvapi sādhanāṅgasya samarthanam / yat kāryaṃ liṅgaṃ kāraṇasya sādhanāyopādīyate, tasya tena saha kāryakāraṇabhāvaprasādhanaṃ bhāvābhāvaprasādhanapramāṇābhyām / yathā - 'idamasmin sati bhavati', 'satsvapi tadanyeṣu samartheṣu taddhetuṣu tadabhāve na bhavati'; iti /
body.translated_text: In the case of a <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-reason) too, there is justification of the proof-member. When an effect is employed as an inferential mark for proving a cause, its causal relation with that [cause] is established through two means of cognition — [one proving] presence and [one proving] absence. As follows: 'This occurs when that is present,' and 'When that is absent, even though other competent causes of it are present, this does not occur.'

body.text: evaṃ hyasyāsandigdhaṃ tatkāryatvaṃ samarthitaṃ bhavati / anyathā kevalaṃ 'tadabhāve na bhavati'; ityupadarśane anyasyāpi tatrābhāve sandigdhamasya sāmarthyam / anyat / tatra samarthaṃ, tadabhāvāt tanna bhūtam /
body.translated_text: For thus its being an effect of that [cause] is justified beyond doubt. Otherwise, by merely showing 'it does not occur in the absence of that,' the capacity [of the proposed cause] remains doubtful since something else also might be absent there. That other [thing] is capable there, [but] due to its absence, that [effect] did not arise.

body.text: etannivṛttau punarnivṛttiryadṛcchāsaṃvādaḥ / mātṛvivāho hi tddeśajanmanaḥ piṇḍakharjūrasya deśāntareṣu mātṛvivāhābhāve 'bhāvavat / evaṃ hi samarthitaṃ tat kāryaṃ sidhyati /
body.translated_text: When that [other factor] is removed, the cessation [of the effect] would be a coincidental agreement. For example, the <s>piṇḍakharjūra</s> (date-palm) born in a particular region [does not grow] in other regions where the mother-marriage [ceremony] is also absent — like [arguing that] the absence [of the palm] is due to the absence of the marriage. Thus, the effect is properly established [only] when so justified.

body.text: siddhiṃ tat svasambhavena tatsambhavaṃ sādhyati, kāryasya kāraṇāvyabhicārāt /
body.translated_text: That [effect], being established, proves the existence of that [cause] by [the principle that] its own occurrence entails the occurrence of that [cause], since an effect does not deviate from its cause.

body.text: avyabhicāre ca svakāraṇaiḥ sarvakāryāṇāṃ sadṛśo nyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And regarding non-deviation [of effects from their causes], the principle is the same for all effects with respect to their own causes.

body.text: evamasamarthanaṃ kāryahetāvapi sādhanāṅgāvacanaṃ tad vādinaḥ parājayasthānam / asamarthite tasmin kāryatvāsiddherarthāntarasya tadbhāvāpratibaddhasvabhāvasya bhāve tadbhāvaniyamābhāvāt, ārabdhārthāsiddhesarvastutaḥ kāryasyāpyupādāne tadapradipādanāt /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the case of a <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-reason) too, non-justification constitutes the non-statement of a proof-member; that is the ground for the proponent's defeat — because when that [effect-nature] is not justified, its being an effect is not established; because when something whose nature is not dependent on that [proposed cause] is present, there is no invariable connection with the presence of that [cause]; because the undertaken purpose is not accomplished; and because even when an actual effect is presented, that [relation] is not demonstrated.

body.text: 9. [anupalabdhāvapi sādhanāṅgasamarthanam]
body.translated_text: 9. [Justification of a proof-member in the case of <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) as well]

body.text: anupalabdhāvapi pratipatturupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhisādhanaṃ samarthanam; tādṛśyā evānupalabdhe rasadvyavahārasiddheḥ / anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya pratipattṛpratyakṣopalabdhinivṛttāvapyabhāvāsiddheḥ /
body.translated_text: In the case of <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) too, the justification is demonstrating the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>); because the convention of non-existence is established only through such [qualified] non-apprehension. Because even when the direct perception of the cognizer or other <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) ceases [to operate on] what does not fulfill the conditions for apprehension, absence is not established.

body.text: tatropalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptiḥ svabhāvaviśeṣaḥ kāraṇāntarasākalyaṃ ca / svabhāvaviśeṣo yanna tribidhena viprakarṣeṇa viprakṛṣṭam / yadanātmarūpapritibhāsavivekena pratipattṛpratyakṣapratibhāsarūpam / tādṛśaḥ satsvanyeṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu tathānupalabdho 'sadvyavahāraviṣayaḥ, anyathā sati liṅge saṃśayaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, 'fulfilling the conditions for apprehension' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>) means having a particular intrinsic nature and the completeness of other causal conditions. The particular intrinsic nature is that which is not remote through any of the three kinds of remoteness. That which, by the distinction between what appears as its own form and what does not, has the form of appearing to the cognizer's direct perception. Such [an object], when the other conditions for apprehension are present and it is thus not apprehended, is a valid object of the convention of non-existence; otherwise, given the [mere] presence of the inferential mark, there would be [only] doubt.

body.text: 10. atrāpi sarvamevaṃvidhamasadvyavahāraviṣaya iti vyāptiḥ, kasyacidasato 'bhyupagame tallakṣaṇāviśeṣāt /
body.translated_text: 10. Here too, the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is: everything of this kind is an object of the convention of non-existence — because if any non-existent [thing] is accepted [as existing despite non-apprehension], there would be no distinguishing mark [to differentiate it from other cases of non-apprehension].

body.text: na hyevaṃvidhasyāsattvānabhyupagame 'nyatra tasya yogaḥ / na hyevaṃvidhasya sataḥ satsvanyeṣūpalambhakāraṇeṣvanupalabdhiḥ / anupalabhyamānaṃ tvīdṛśaṃ nāstītyetā - vanmātranimitto 'yamasadvyavahāraḥ, anyasya tannimittasyābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: For if the non-existence of something of this kind is not accepted, there is no scope for it elsewhere. For there is no non-apprehension of something existing that is of this kind when the other conditions for apprehension are present. But what is of this kind and not apprehended is simply non-existent — this alone is the basis of the convention of non-existence, since there is no other basis for that convention.

body.text: 11. sarvasāmarthyaviveko nimittamiti cet / evametat, tasyaiva sarvasāmarthyavivekina evaṃ pratītiḥ, anyasya tatpratipattyupāyasyābhāvāt / tatpratipattau ca satyāmasadvyavahāra itīdaṃ tannimittamucyate /
body.translated_text: 11. If [one objects that] the distinguishing of all capacities is the basis [of the non-existence convention] — indeed so; it is precisely of such [an object], one that is distinguished from all capacities, that there is such a cognition, because there is no other means of cognizing it. And when that cognition occurs, the convention of non-existence [follows] — this is what is stated as its basis.

body.text: 12. buddhivyapadeśārthakriyābhyaḥ sadvyavahāro viparyaye cāsadvyavahāra iti cet / bhavati buddheryathoktapratibhāsāyāḥ sadvyavahāraḥ, viparyaye 'sadvyavahāraḥ /
body.translated_text: 12. If [one says that] the convention of existence arises from cognition, verbal designation, and causal efficacy, and the convention of non-existence from their contraries — [we reply:] yes, the convention of existence arises from cognition that appears as described, and the convention of non-existence from its contrary.

body.text: pratyakṣāviṣaye tu syālliṅgajāyā api kutaścit sadvyavahāraḥ /
body.translated_text: However, in what is beyond the range of direct perception, the convention of existence may arise even from inferential cognition based on some [evidence].

body.text: asadvyavahārastu tadviparyaye 'naikāntikaḥ, viprakṛṣṭe 'rthe pratipattṛpratyakṣasya anyasya vā pramāṇasya nivṛttāvapi saṃśayāt /
body.translated_text: But the convention of non-existence in the contrary case is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because even when the cognizer's direct perception or other <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) ceases [to function] regarding a remote object, doubt [remains].

body.text: 13. na ca sarve buddhivyapadeśāstadbhedābhedau vā vastusattāṃ vastubhedābhedasattāṃ vā sādhayanti, astsvapi kathañcidatītānāgatādiṣu nānaikārthakriyākāriṣu vārtheṣu tadbhāvakhyāpanāya nānaikātmatābhāve 'pinānaikarūpāṇāṃ vṛtteḥ - rājā mahāsammataḥ (

children.text: ) prabhavo rājavaṃśasya, saṅkhaścakravartī mahāsammatanirmitasya yūpasyotthāpayitā, śaśaviṣāṇaṃ, rūpaṃ sanidarśanaṃ sapratighaṃ ghaṭaśceti /
children.translated_text: was the progenitor of the royal lineage; <s>Saṅkha</s> the <s>Cakravartin</s> was the raiser of the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) fashioned by <s>Mahāsammata</s>; the horn of a hare; form is visible and tangible; and a pot' — and so forth.

body.translated_text: 13. Nor do all cognitions and verbal designations, or their identity and difference, establish real existence or the existence of real identity and difference, since even among things that exist in some manner — such as past and future entities, or things that do not perform one and the same causal function — [cognitions and designations] operate despite the absence of a single nature and despite the absence of a single form, [as in the expressions:] 'The king <s>Mahāsammata</s>

body.text: 14. nahi sanidarśanādiśabdā nānāvastuviṣayāḥ, ekatropasaṃhārāt /
body.translated_text: 14. For the words 'visible' and the like are not about multiple real entities, since they are applied collectively to one [entity].

body.text: nānāviṣayatve 'pyekatropasaṃhārastannimittānāṃ tattatsamavāyāditi cet / āyāse batāyaṃ tapasvī padārthe [padarthaḥ?] patito 'nekasambandhinamupakṛtyānekaṃśabdamātmani tebhyaḥ samāśaṃsan ! sa yaiḥ śaktibhedairanekasambandhina mupakaroti tairevānekaṃ śabdaṃ kiṃ notthāpayati ! evaṃ hyanena pramparānusārapariśramaḥ parihṛto bhavati /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'Though having different objects, the gathering together in one [entity] is due to the inherence of their respective causes in their respective [loci].' [Reply:] Alas, this poor ascetic has fallen into needless effort regarding the [composite] object—having helped the entity that has many relations, and attributing many words from those [relations] to itself! By those very distinctions of power through which it helps the many-related [thing], why does it not raise up many words? For thus the labor of tracing the chain [of inference] would be avoided.

body.text: nānāśabdotthāpanāsāmarthye nānāsambandhyupakāro 'pi mā bhūt, anupakāre hi teṣāṃ tatsambandhitāpi na sidhyati / ghaṭa ityapi ca rūpādaya eva bahava ekārthakriyākāriṇa ekaśabdavācyā bhavantu, kimarthāntarakalpanayā?
body.translated_text: If [the entity is] incapable of raising up multiple words, then its assistance to the many-related [things] should also not exist; for without assistance, their being so related is not established either. And in [the word] 'pot' (<s>ghaṭa</s>), just the many [qualities like] form etc., producing a single causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), may be expressible by a single word—what need is there for imagining another entity?

body.text: bahavo 'pi hi ekārthakāriṇo bhaveyuḥ, cakṣurādivat / tatsāmarthyakhyāpanāya tatraikaśabdaniyogo 'pi syāditi yuktaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: For even many things may produce a single causal efficacy, like the eye etc. And we consider it reasonable that a single word may be assigned to them in order to make known that capacity.

body.text: 15. na ca niṣprayojanā lokasyārtheṣu śabdayojanā / tatra ye 'rthāḥ saha pṛthagvā ekaprayojanāḥ teṣāṃ tadbhāvakhyāpanāya hi ekśabdo niyujyeta yadi, kiṃ syāt? tadarthakriyāśaktikhyāpanāya niyuktasya samudāyaśabdasyaikavacanavirodho 'pi nāstyeva; sahitānāṃ sā śaktirekā, na pratyekamiti /
body.translated_text: 15. The convention of people assigning words to objects is not purposeless. If a single word were to be assigned to those objects that, together or separately, have a single purpose, in order to make known their existence—what would [be wrong]? There is no contradiction with the singular number for the composite word (<s>samudāya-śabda</s>) assigned to make known the capacity for causal efficacy; for the capacity of the combined [elements] is one, not individual.

body.text: samudāyaśabda ekasmin samudāye vācye ekavacanaṃ ghaṭa iti /
body.translated_text: The composite word uses the singular 'pot' (<s>ghaṭa</s>) when referring to a single composite.

body.text: jātiśabdeṣvarthānāṃ pratyekaṃ sahitānāṃ ca śaktirnānaikā ca śaktiriti, nānaikaśaktivivakṣāyāṃ bahuvacanamekavacanaṃ cecchātaḥ, vṛkṣā vṛkṣamiti [? vṛkṣa iti] syāt /
body.translated_text: In the case of class-terms (<s>jāti-śabda</s>), the capacity of objects individually and combined is neither one nor many; when wishing to express the [capacity that is] neither one nor many, the plural or singular is used at will—'trees' (<s>vṛkṣāḥ</s>) or 'tree' (<s>vṛkṣa</s>).

body.text: yadyeṣa niyamo bahuṣveva bahuvacanam ekasminnekavacanamiti /
body.translated_text: If this is the rule—that plural is [used] for many and singular for one—

body.text: asmākaṃ tu sāṅketikeṣvartheṣu saṅketavaśāt tāvitya bhiniveśa eva /
body.translated_text: For us, however, regarding conventional objects, due to convention, there is merely this much attachment.

body.text: 16. nāneko rūpādirekaśabdotthāpane samartha iti cet / kiṃ vai puruṣavṛtteranapekṣāḥ śabdānarthaḥ svayamutthyāpayanti, āhosvit puruṣaiḥ śabdā vyavahārārthamartheṣu niyujyante? svayamutthāpane hi bhāvaśaktiḥ, āśaktirvā cintyeta / na ca tadyuktam, puruṣaisteṣāṃ niyoge yatheṣṭaṃ niyuñjīranniti kastatropānambhaḥ?
body.translated_text: 16. [Objection:] 'No plurality [like] form etc. is capable of raising up a single word.' [Reply:] Do objects themselves raise up words independently of human activity, or are words assigned to objects by people for the purpose of communication? If [objects] raise [words] by themselves, one would have to consider either their inherent power or capacity. But that is not correct; when people make the assignment, they would assign as they wish—what obstacle is there?

body.text: nimittaṃ ca niyogasyoktameva /
body.translated_text: And the reason for assignment has already been stated.

body.text: api ca - yadi na rūpādīnāmekena śabdena sambandhaḥ, kathamekenaiṣā - māśrayābhimatena dravyeṇa sambandha iti kevalamayamasadbhūtābhiniveśa eva /
body.translated_text: Moreover—if form etc. have no connection with a single word, how can this be [maintained]—their connection with a single preferred substance (<s>dravya</s>)? This is merely a groundless attachment.

body.text: na vayamekasambandhavirodhādekaṃ śabdaṃ necchāmaḥ, api tvabhinnānāṃ rūpādīnāṃ ghaṭakambalādiṣu nānārthakriyāśabdavirodhāt te ekarūpāḥ samudāyāntarā - sambhāvinīmarthakriyāmeva na kuryuḥ, tena tatprakāśanāyaikenāpi śabdenocyeran /
body.translated_text: We do not reject a single word because of a contradiction in single relation; rather, because of the contradiction of multiple causal efficacies and words for undifferentiated form etc. in pots, blankets, and so forth, those [elements] being of uniform nature would not produce the causal efficacy possible in other composites; therefore they could be expressed by a single word to reveal that [particular efficacy].

body.text: bhavatu nāma kasyacidiyaṃ vāñchā - bhaveyurekarūpā rūpādayaḥ sarvasamudāyeṣu iti / kimidaṃ parasparaviviktarūpapratibhāsādhyakṣadarśanamenāmupekṣate?
body.translated_text: Let someone wish: 'May form etc. be of uniform nature in all composites.' Does this [person] disregard the evidence of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), which reveals forms as mutually distinct in appearance?

body.text: aniṣṭaṃ cedaṃ rūpādīnā / pratisamudāyaṃ svabhāvabhedopagamāt /
body.translated_text: This is undesirable for form etc., because of the acceptance of difference of nature in each composite.

body.text: 17. yadyanya eva rūpādibhyo ghaṭaḥ syāt kiṃ syāt?
body.translated_text: 17. If the pot were something other than form etc., what would [follow]?

body.text: astu, tasya pratyakṣasya sato 'rūpādirūpasya tadvivekena buddhau svarūpeṇa pratibhāsane kimāvaraṇam?
body.translated_text: Let it be so. Since that perceptual [entity] exists and has a nature different from form etc., what prevents its appearing in cognition in its own form, distinct from them?

body.text: pratibhāsamānāśca vivekena pratyakṣārthā dṛśyante 'pṛthagdeśatve 'pigandharasādayaḥ. vātātapasparśādayaścaikendriyagrāhyatve 'pi /
body.translated_text: And objects of perception that appear distinctly are seen [as separate] even when not in different locations—[such as] smell, taste, and so forth. And [so too] wind, heat, and touch, even when graspable by a single sense organ.

body.text: idameva ca pratyakṣasya pratyakṣatvaṃ yadanātmarūpādivivekena svarūpasya buddhau samarpaṇam / ayaṃ punarghaṭādiramūlyadānakrayī yaḥ svarūpaṃ ca nopadarśayati, pratyakṣatāṃ ca svīkartumicchati /
body.translated_text: And this alone is the perceptuality of a perceptual [entity]—that it presents its own form in cognition, distinct from what is not its own nature. But this pot etc. is a buyer who pays no price: it neither displays its own form, yet wishes to claim perceptuality.

body.text: 18. etena buddhiśabdādayo 'pi vyākhyātāḥ, yadi taistatsādhanamiṣyate / na ca pratyakṣasyānabhibhave rūpānupalakṣaṇam; yena tatsādhanāya liṅgamucyate / apratyakṣatve 'pyapramāṇasya sattopagamo na yuktaḥ / tanna rūpādibhyo 'nyo ghaṭaḥ evaṃ tāvanna buddhivyapadeśābhyāṃ sattāvyavahāraḥ, sattābhedābhedavyavahāro vā / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vādanyāya</s> 22]
Therefore, from the reversal of that, [the reversal follows].

body.translated_text: 18. By this, cognition, language, etc. are also explained, if proof [of composite entities] is sought through them. When perception is not overpowered, there is no non-apprehension of form; hence no inferential mark is stated for proving that [composite entity]. Even in the case of non-perceptuality, it is not proper to accept the existence of what has no means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Therefore the pot is not other than form etc. Thus, the existence-convention is not [established] through cognition and designation, nor [is the convention of] identity and difference of existence.

body.text: 19. arthakriyātastu sattāvyavahāraḥ syāt, na sattābhedābhedavyavahāraḥ, ekasyāpyanekārthakriyādarśanāt / yathā pradīpasya vijñānavartivikārajvālāntarotpādanāni / anekasyāpi cakṣurāderekavijñānakriyādarśanāt /
body.translated_text: 19. From causal efficacy, the convention of existence may [be established], but not the convention of identity or difference of existence, because even of a single [entity], multiple causal efficacies are observed. As, for example, a lamp produces consciousness, wick-transformation, and flame-succession. And even of many [entities] like the eye etc., a single cognitive activity is observed.

body.text: na brūmaḥ - arthakriyābhedamātreṇa sattābheda iti / kiṃ tarhi? adṛṣṭārthakriyābhedena / yā arthakriyā yasminnadṛṣṭā punardṛśyate sā sattābhedaṃ sādhayati / yathā mṛdyadṛṣṭā satyudakadhāraṇādyarthakriyā ghaṭe dṛśyamānā / adṛṣṭā ca tantuṣu prāvaraṇādyarthakriyā paṭe dṛsyate iti sattābhedaḥ /
body.translated_text: We do not say that mere difference of causal efficacy [establishes] difference of existence. What then? [Difference is established] by an unseen causal efficacy. A causal efficacy that was unseen in one [thing] but is then seen [in another]—that establishes difference of existence. As, for example, the causal efficacy of holding water etc., unseen in clay, is seen in the pot. And the causal efficacy of covering etc., unseen in threads, is seen in cloth—hence [there is] difference of existence.

body.text: sidhyatyevamarthāntaraṃ, tathāpyavayavī na sidhyati / yathāpratyayaṃ saṃskārasantatau svabhāvabhedo tpatterarthakriyābhedaḥ / araṇinirmathanāvasthādāvivāgneḥ sthūlakarīṣatṛṇakāṣṭhadahanaśaktibhedaḥ, tathā yathāpratyayaṃ svabhāvabhedotpattestantvādiṣvarthakriyābhedaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus a different entity is established. Nevertheless, a composite whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is not established. For the difference of causal efficacy arises from the difference of nature arising in accordance with [different] conditions in the continuum of impressions (<s>saṃskāra-santati</s>). Just as the different capacities of fire to burn large cow-dung, grass, and wood [arise] from the conditions beginning with the rubbing of fire-sticks, so too the difference of causal efficacy in threads etc. [arises] from the difference of nature arising in accordance with conditions.

body.text: etena buddhivyapadeśabhedābhedau vyākhyātau /
body.translated_text: By this, identity and difference of cognition and designation are also explained.

body.text: 20. tatrayaduktam - 'arthakriyātaḥ sattāvyavahārasiddhiḥ, viparyayād viparyayaḥ'; iti; satyametat / sa eva tu viparyayo 'nupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteṣu na sidhyati /
body.translated_text: 20. Regarding what was said—'From causal efficacy, the convention of existence is established; from the reverse, the reverse'—this is true. But that very reverse is not established in the case of things that meet the conditions for being apprehensible (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>).

body.text: tatra punaridamanicchato 'pyāyātam - 'yasyedaṃ sāmarthyamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sannopalabhyate, so 'sadvyavahāraviṣayaḥ, sāmarthyalakṣaṇatvāt sattvasya'; iti /
body.translated_text: Then this [conclusion] comes even to one unwilling: 'That which, meeting the conditions for being apprehensible, is not apprehended when existing—that is the object of the non-existence convention, because existence has the nature of [causal] capacity.'

body.text: tathāpi ko 'tiśayaḥ pūrvakādasya? na hi svabhāvādarthāntaraṃ sāmarthyam / tasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya yo 'nupalambhaḥ sa svabhāvasyaiveti pūrvakaiveyamanupalabdhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Even so, what improvement is this over the former [formulation]? For capacity is not something different from the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). The non-apprehension of that which meets the conditions for apprehension is [non-apprehension] of the intrinsic nature itself—so this is the very same non-apprehension as before.

body.text: tasmādanena kvacit keṣāñcidasadvyavahāramabhyupagacchatā ato 'nupalambhādabhyupagantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, one who, by means of this [argument], accepts the non-existence convention of certain [things] in certain [places], must accept it on the basis of this non-apprehension.

body.text: so 'nyatrāpi tathāvidhe 'viśiṣṭa iti so 'pi tathāstu iti / na vā kvacid, viśeṣābhāvāt / vyāptiḥ - sarva evaṃvidho 'nupalabdho 'sadvyavahāraviṣaya iti /
body.translated_text: And that [non-apprehension], being no different in other [cases] of the same kind, should be [accepted] in those [cases] too. Or [it should apply] to no case at all, because of the absence of distinction. The pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) [is]: every entity of this kind, when not apprehended, is an object of the non-existence convention.

body.text: 21. naiva kaścit kvacit kathañcidanupalabdho 'pyasadvyavahāraviṣaya iti cet / sarvasya sarvarūpāṇāṃ sarvadānivṛtteḥ sarvaṃ sarvatra sarvadā samupayujyeta /
body.translated_text: 21. [Objection:] 'No [entity] whatever, anywhere, in any way, even when not apprehended, is an object of the non-existence convention.' [Reply:] Since there is no cessation of all forms of everything at all times, everything would be useful everywhere at all times.

body.text: idaṃ ca na syāt - 'idamataḥ', 'nāta idam', 'ihedam', 'iha nedam', 'idānīmidam', 'idānīṃ nedam', 'idamevam'; 'idaṃ naivam'; iti; kasyacidapi rūpasya kathañcit kvacit kadācid viviktahetorabhāvāt / ananvayavyatirekaṃ viśvaṃ syāt, bhedābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: And the following distinctions would not hold: 'this from here,' 'not this from here,' 'this here,' 'not this here,' 'this now,' 'not this now,' 'this thus,' 'not this thus'—because there would be no cause of distinction of any form whatsoever anywhere at any time. The universe would be without positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), due to the absence of difference.

body.text: avasthānivṛttipravṛttibhedebhyo vyavastheti cet / nanvata eva sarvaviṣayasyāsadvyavahārasyābhāvānna te sambhavanti, yatastebhyo vyavasthā syāt /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'Determination [comes] from the differences of states, cessation, and activity.' [Reply:] But precisely because there is no non-existence convention regarding anything whatsoever, those [differences] are impossible, from which determination would arise.

body.text: kvacid viṣaye 'sadvyavahāropagame sa kuta iti vaktavyam / na hyanupalambhādanyo vyavacchedaheturasti; vidhipratiṣedhābhyaṃ vyavacchede sarvadānupalambhasyaiva sādhanatvāt /
body.translated_text: If the non-existence convention is accepted regarding some object, its cause must be stated. For there is no cause of exclusion other than non-apprehension; since in exclusion through affirmation and negation, non-apprehension alone is always the proof.

body.text: anupalambhādeva tadabhyupagame, sa yatraivāsti sarvo 'sadvyavahāraviṣaya iti vaktavyam, viśeṣābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: If it is accepted [that the non-existence convention arises] from non-apprehension alone, then wherever [non-apprehension] exists, everything must be stated to be the object of the non-existence convention, due to the absence of distinction.

body.text: 22. sarvapramāṇanivṛttiranupalabdhiḥ / sā yatra so 'sadviṣaya [? so 'sadvyavahāra- viṣaya] iṣṭa iti cet / sukumāraprajño devānāmpriyo na sahate pramāṇacintā - parikleśaṃ, yena nātrādaraṃ kṛtavān /
body.translated_text: 22. [Objection:] 'Non-apprehension is the cessation of all means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Where that [cessation] occurs, that [thing] is accepted as the object of the non-existence convention.' [Reply:] The tender-minded one, dear to the gods, cannot endure the fatigue of pondering the means of valid cognition, and therefore has paid no regard [to this matter].

body.text: na hyanumānādinivṛttirabhāvaṃ gamayati, vyabhicārāt / na sarvapratyakṣanivṛttiḥ, asiddheḥ /
body.translated_text: For the cessation of inference etc. does not lead to [proof of] non-existence, because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). And the cessation of all perception is unestablished.

body.text: nātmapratyakṣāviśeṣanivṛttirapi viprakṛṣṭeṣu /
body.translated_text: Nor [is it established that there is] cessation of [all] perception without distinction, in the case of distant [objects].

body.text: tasmāt svabhāvaviśeṣo yataḥ pramāṇānniyamen sadvyavahāraṃ pratipadyate, tannivṛttistasyāsadvyavahāraṃ sādhayati, tatsvabhāvasattāyāḥ tatpramāṇāsattayā iṣṭeḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, the particular intrinsic nature that, from a [specific] means of valid cognition, invariably receives the convention of existence—the cessation of that [means of valid cognition] establishes the convention of non-existence for it, because the existence of that nature is accepted as contingent upon the existence of that means of valid cognition.

body.text: na copalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyārthasyāpraptyakṣādanyopalabdhiḥ, yenānumānādasyopalabdhiḥ syāt / na ca tadrūpānyathābhāvamantareṇāpratyakṣatā, anyathābhāve ca tadeva na syāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there any apprehension other than direct perception of an object that has attained the conditions for apprehension, such that its apprehension by inference would follow. And without the otherness of its nature, there is no imperceptibility; and the otherness of its nature would not be possible without the otherness of the nature [of the object itself].

body.text: api ca - kuta idamamantrauṣadhamindrajānaṃ bhāvena śikṣitam, yadayamajātānaṣṭarūpātiśayo 'vyavadhānadūrasthānastasyaiva tadavasthendriyādereva puruṣasya kadācit pratyakṣaḥ, apratyakṣaśca; yena kadācidasyānumānamupalabdhiḥ, kadācit pratyakṣaṃ, kadācidāgamaḥ ! ekasminnevānatiśaye amīṣāṃ prakārāṇāṃ virodhāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover — whence comes this [thing], not [produced by] spells, herbs, or magic, trained by its very nature, such that this [entity], whose excellence is unborn and unperished, being not obstructed and not remote in position, is perceived by a person with that very kind of organ and so on?

body.text: 23. nānatiśayanivṛttyā, [naikātiśayanivṛtyā?] aparātiśayotpattyā ca tairvyavahārabhedopagamāt /
body.translated_text: 23. [This is] not because of the cessation of one excellence alone, or because of the arising of another excellence, since they [the opponents] accept a difference in conventional usage based on these.

body.text: so 'tiśayastasyātmabhūto 'nanvaye [... nanvayaḥ?] nivartamānaḥ pravartamānaśca kathaṃ na svabhāvanānātvamākarṣayati, sukhaduḥkhavat / sānvayatve ca kā kasya pravṛttirnivṛttirvā iti yatkiñcidetat /
body.translated_text: That excellence, being of the very nature of that [substance] — ceasing and arising without continuity — how does it not bring about a real plurality of natures, like pleasure and pain? And if there is continuity, what is the difference?

body.text: athavā yadi ca kasyacitsvabhāvasya pravṛttirnivṛttirveti svayamapyabhyanujñāyate, tadetadeva paro bruvāṇāḥ kimiti nānumanyate?
body.translated_text: Alternatively, if it is conceded by you yourself that some nature arises and ceases, then why is it not accepted when the opponent says this very same thing?

body.text: tasya niranvayopajananavināśopagamāditi cet /
body.translated_text: If it be said: because their arising and destruction are accepted as without continuity —

body.text: ko 'yamanvayo nāma? bhāvasya janmavināśayoḥ śaktiḥ; sāstyeva prāgapi janmano nirodhādapyūrdhvam / tenāyaṃ nāpūrvaḥ sarvathā jāyate, na pūrvo vinaśyatīti /
body.translated_text: What is this 'continuity' (<s>anvaya</s>)? It is the capacity (<s>śakti</s>) of an entity for birth and destruction. And that [capacity] exists even before birth and after cessation as well. Therefore this [thing] is not entirely unprecedented when it arises, nor does a prior [thing] perish entirely.

body.text: yadi sā sarvadānatiśayā, kimidānīmatiśayavad yatkṛto 'yaṃ vyavahāravibhāgaḥ?
body.translated_text: If that [capacity] is always without excellence, then what is the basis for this conventional distinction made as if there were excellence?

body.text: tā avasthā atiśayavatya iti cet, tā avasthāḥ sā ca śaktiḥ kimeko bhavaḥ? āhosvit nānā?
body.translated_text: If it be said: those states possess excellence — then are those states and that capacity one entity or different?

body.text: ekaścet kathamidānīmidamekatrāvibhaktātmani niṣparyāyaṃ parasparavyāhataṃ yokṣyate - janmājanma, nivṛttiranivṛttiḥ, ekatvaṃ nānātvaṃ, pratyakṣatāpratyakṣatā, arthakriyopayogaḥ anupayogaścetyādi /
body.translated_text: If one — then how will these mutually contradictory [properties] be simultaneously and indiscriminately joined in a single undivided entity: birth and non-birth, cessation and non-cessation, oneness and plurality, perceptibility and imperceptibility?

body.text: 24. asti paryāyo 'vasthā śaktiriti, tenāvirodha iti cet / vismaraṇaśīlo devānāmpriyaḥ prakaraṇaṃ na lakṣayati / śaktiravasthetyeko bhāvo 'vibhāga iti yat ko 'yaṃ virodha uktaḥ?
body.translated_text: 24. If it be said: there is a succession — states and capacity — and hence no contradiction — the 'dear friend of the gods' (the opponent), being forgetful, does not notice the [original] topic of discussion. For 'capacity' and 'state' are one entity, undivided — this was [the very thesis].

body.text: athāpyanayorvibhāgaḥ, nakaścid virodhaḥ, kevalaṃ sānvayau bhāvasya janmavināśau iti na syāt /
body.translated_text: Even if there were a division between these two, there would be no contradiction. However, [then] it would not follow that the birth and destruction of an entity have continuity.

body.text: tasmād yasyānvayo na tasya janmavināsau, yasya ca tau na tasyānvayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, that which has continuity does not have birth and destruction; and that which has those does not have continuity.

body.text: tayorabhedādadoṣa iti ced, anuttaraṃ bata doṣasaṅkaṭamatrabhavān dṛṣṭirāgeṇa pravesyamāno 'pi nātmānaṃ / cetayati / abhedo hi nāmaikyam, 'tau'; ityayaṃ ca bhedādhiṣṭhāno bhāviko vyavahāraḥ / nivṛttiprādurbhāvayoḥ anivṛttiprādurbhāvau, sthitāvasthitiḥ ityādikaṃ nānātvalakṣaṇaṃ ca kathaṃ yotsyate?
body.translated_text: If it be said: there is no fault due to their non-difference — ah, the 'dear friend of the gods,' being driven by dogmatic attachment into a hopeless tangle of faults, does not even perceive himself [in this predicament]! For non-difference means identity. 'These two' — this [very expression indicates duality].

body.text: atha hi bhāvānāṃ bheda etadvirahaścābhedaḥ, yathā - sukhādiṣu śaktyavasthayoccaikātmani / anyathā bhedābhedalakṣaṇābhāvād bhedābhedayoravyavasthā syātsarvatra /
body.translated_text: But if the difference of entities is this, and the absence of this is non-difference — as in the case of capacity and states in pleasure and the like, which are of one nature — then otherwise, in the absence of the defining characteristics of difference and non-difference, there would be no ascertainment of difference and non-difference.

body.text: tadātmani prādurbhāvo 'bhedaḥ, viparyaye bhedaḥ, yathā - mṛdātmani prādurbhavato ghaṭasya tasmādabhedaḥ, bhedaśca viparyaye sukhaduḥkhayoriti idaṃ bhedābhedalakṣaṇaṃ, tenāvirodha iti cet /
body.translated_text: Manifestation in the nature of that is non-difference; in the contrary case, difference — as, for example, the pot manifesting in the nature of clay is non-different from it, while pleasure and pain are different [from each other]. This is the definition of difference and non-difference.

body.text: na vai mṛdātmani ghaṭasya prādurbhāvaḥ / kiṃ tarhi? mṛdātmaiva kaścid ghaṭaḥ, na hyekastrailokye mṛdātmā / prativijñaptipratibhāsabhedaśca dravyasvabhāvabhedāt / evaṃ hyasyāpi sukhādiṣu caitanyeṣu bhedāvagamaḥ samartho bhavati /
body.translated_text: It is not the case that the pot manifests in the nature of clay. Rather, some [particular] clay-natured thing is a pot — for there is not a single clay-nature in the three worlds. And the difference in appearance in each cognition pertains to the inherent nature of the substance.

body.text: yadyeva, bhedaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If so, then there would be difference.

body.text: satyapyetasmin kasyacidātmano 'nvayā devamiti cet / sukhādiṣvapyayaṃ prasaṅgaḥ caitanyeṣu ca /
body.translated_text: If it be said: even granted this, the continuity of some [underlying] nature [would be maintained] — then the same consequence applies to pleasure and the like, and to conscious entities as well.

body.text: na ca ghaṭādiṣvapi sarvātmanānvayaḥ, avaiśvarūpyasahotpattyādiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there continuity in all respects even in pots and the like, for there would follow the absurd consequence of dissimilarity in nature, simultaneous arising, and so on.

body.text: na ca ghaṭaṃ mṛdātmānaṃ ca kaścid vivekenopalakṣayati, yenaivaṃ syādidamiha prādurbhūtamiti /
body.translated_text: Nor does anyone perceive a pot and a clay-nature as distinct, such that one could say 'this has manifested here.'

body.text: na hyadhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhāninorvivekenānupalakṣaṇe evaṃ bhavati / na ca śakteḥ śaktyātmani prādurbhāvaḥ iti tasyāḥ svātmano 'bhedo na syāt /
body.translated_text: For when there is no perception of distinctness between substratum and supervenient, such [a statement] is not possible. And the capacity does not manifest in the nature of capacity itself, so there would be no non-difference of it from its own self.

body.text: 25. etenaiva pariṇāmaḥ pratyuktaḥ / yo 'pi hi kalpayed - 'yo yasya pariṇāmaḥ sa tasmādabhinnaḥ'; iti / na hi śaktirātmanaḥ pariṇāma iti /
body.translated_text: 25. By this very [argument], transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is also refuted. Even if someone were to postulate: 'that which is a transformation of something is non-different from it' — capacity is not a transformation of itself.

body.text: kiñcedamuktaṃ bhavati - pariṇāma ityavasthitasya dravyasya dharmāntaranivṛttiḥ, dharmāntaraprādurbhavaśca pariṇāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, what has been said amounts to this: transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) means the cessation of one property and the manifestation of another property of an established substance.

body.text: yattaddharmāntaraṃ nivartate prādurbhavati ca, kiṃ tat tadevāvasthitaṃ dravyaṃ syāt, tato 'rthāntaraṃ vā, anyavikalpābhāvat?
body.translated_text: That other property which ceases and manifests — is it the very same established substance, or something different from it? There being no other alternative —

body.text: yadi tattadeva, tasyāvasthānānna nivṛttiprādurbhāvāviti kasya tāviti vaktavyam /
body.translated_text: If it is that very [substance], then since it persists, there would be no cessation or manifestation — and whose [cessation or manifestation] would that be?

body.text: avasthitasya dharmāntaramiti ca na sidhyati / na hi tadeva tasyānapāśritavyapekṣābhedaṃ dharmāntaraṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: And 'another property of the established [substance]' is not established. For that very thing does not become another property of itself without dependence on a relation of being non-independent.

body.text: atha dravyādarthāntaraṃ dharmaḥ, tadā tasya nivṛttiprādurbhāvābhyaṃ na dravyasya pariṇatiḥ / na hyarthāntaragatābhyāṃ syāt nivṛttiprādurbhāvābhyāmarthāntarasya pariṇatiḥ, caitanye 'pi prasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: If, however, the property is something different from the substance, then through its cessation and manifestation, there is no transformation of the substance. For through the cessation and manifestation occurring in something different, there would be no transformation of another thing.

body.text: dravyasya dharma iti ca vyapadeśo na sidhyati, sambandhābhāvāt / na hi kāryakāraṇabhāvādanyo vastusambandho 'sti /
body.translated_text: And the designation 'property of the substance' is not established, due to the absence of a relation. For there is no real relation between entities other than the causal relation.

body.text: na cānayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ, svayamatadātmano 'tatkāraṇatvāt, dharmasya dravyādarthāntarabhūtatvāt /
body.translated_text: And there is no causal relation between these two, because what is not of the nature of that is not the cause of that, since the property is something different from the substance.

body.text: arthāntaratve 'pi dharmakāraṇatve, arthāntarasya kāryasyotpādanāt dravyasya pariṇāmaḥ itīṣṭaṃ syāt / tadviruddhasyāpi hetuphalasantāne mṛddravyākhye, pūrvakānmṛtpiṇḍadravyāt kāraṇāduttarasya ghaṭadravyasya kāryasyotpattau 'mṛd dravyaṃ pariṇatam'; iti vyavahārasyopagamāt /
body.translated_text: Even if, while being something different, [the substance] were the cause of the property — since it would be producing an effect that is something different, the desired [conclusion] that 'the transformation belongs to the substance' would follow. But even for what is contrary to that, in the causal continuum called 'clay-substance,' [the same logic applies].

body.text: na ca dharmasya dravyāt tattvānyatvābhyāmanyo vikalpaḥ sambhavati, ubhayathā yena pariṇāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: And no alternative other than identity or difference of the property with respect to the substance is possible — by either of which transformation [would be established].

body.text: 26. na nirvivekandravyameva dharmaḥ, nāpi dravyādarthāntaram, kiṃ tarhi? dravyasya sanniveśo 'vasthāntaram, yathā aṅgulīnāṃ muṣṭiḥ / na hyaṅulya eva nirvivekā muṣṭiḥ, prasāritānāmamuṣṭitvāt /
body.translated_text: 26. A property is not the substance itself without distinction, nor is it something different from the substance. Rather, it is a configuration (<s>sanniveśa</s>) of the substance, another state — just as a fist is [a configuration] of fingers. For the fingers are not nothing other than a fist.

body.text: nāpyarthāntaraṃ, pṛthaksvabhāvānnopalabdhiriti cet / na, muṣṭeraṅguliviśeṣatvāt / aṅgulya eva hi kāścana muṣṭiḥ, na tu sarvāḥ / na hi prasāritā aṅgulyo nirvivekasvabhāvāḥ muṣṭyaṅgulyaḥ, avasthādvaye 'pi ubhayapratipattiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: If it be said: nor is [the fist] something different [from the fingers], because it is not perceived as having a separate nature — no, because the fist is a specific [configuration] of fingers. For only certain fingers [arranged in a certain way] constitute a fist, not all [configurations of fingers]. For extended fingers are not a fist.

body.text: yatra cahi khalu vivekaḥ svabhābhūtaḥ, sa eava vastubhedalakṣaṇaṃ sukhuduḥkhavat /
body.translated_text: And wherever distinction is inherent in the nature [of the thing], that alone is the mark of real difference, as with pleasure and pain.

body.text: parabhūte ca vivekotpāde 'ṅgulyaḥ prasāritā evopalabhyeran / na hi svayaṃ svabhāvādapracyutasyārthāntarotpāde 'nyathopalabdhi ratiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: And when distinction arises as extrinsic, the fingers would be perceived as merely extended. For when something has not departed from its own nature, if something different arises, there is no occasion for it to be perceived differently.

body.text: nanūktaṃ, 'dravyameva nirvivekamavasthā, nāpi dravyādarthāntaram'; iti /
body.translated_text: But it was said: 'A state is the substance itself without distinction, and it is also not something different from the substance.'

body.text: uktamidaṃ, na punaryuktam / na hi sato vastunastattvānyatve muktvā anyaḥ prakāraḥ sambhavati, tayorvastuni paraspara parihārasthitilakṣaṇatvenaikatyāgasyāparopādānanāntarīyakatvāt /
body.translated_text: This was stated but is not cogent. For no mode of being other than identity and difference is possible for a real entity — since these two, being defined by mutual exclusion in reality, [entail that] the abandonment of one necessarily leads to the ascertainment of the other.

body.text: aṅgulīṣu punaḥ pratikṣaṇavināśinīṣvanyā eva prasaritaḥ anyā muṣṭiḥ /
body.translated_text: In the case of fingers, however, since they perish at every moment, those that are extended are entirely different from those that form a fist.

body.text: tatra muṣṭyādiśabdā viśeṣaviṣayāḥ, aṅgulīśabdaḥ sāmānyaviṣayaḥ, bījāṅkurādiśabdavat, vrīhyādiśabdavacca / tenāṅgulyaḥ prasāritā na muṣṭiḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, words like 'fist' and the like have specific [configurations] as their referent, while the word 'fingers' has the general as its referent — like the words 'seed,' 'sprout,' and so on, and like the word 'rice.' Therefore, fingers that are extended are not a fist.

body.text: 27. tadyadi prāgasadeva kāraṇe kāryaṃ bhavet, kiṃ na sarvaḥ sarvasmāt bhabvati, na hyasattve kaścid viśeṣa iti?
body.translated_text: 27. Now then, if the effect were entirely non-existent (<s>asat</s>) in the cause prior [to its production], why would not everything arise from everything? For in non-existence, there is no distinction whatsoever.

body.text: nanu sarvatra sattve 'pyayaṃ tulyo doṣaḥ - na hi sattve kaścid viśeṣaḥ, viśeṣe vā sa viśeṣa straigunyād bhinnaḥ syāt, tadbhāve viśeṣasyānanvayāt /
body.translated_text: But even if there is existence everywhere, this same objection applies equally — for in existence there is no distinction. Or if there were such a distinction, it would be different from the three <s>guṇas</s>; and if such [a distinction] existed, it would follow that the [particular] distinction has no continuity.

body.text: sataśca sarvātmanā niḥsvabhāvāvasthāyāmiva kiṃ jāyate? sādhanavaiphalyaṃ ca, sādhyasya kasyacidabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: And when what exists is in a state utterly devoid of own-nature, as it were — what is born? And the means of attainment would be futile, since there is nothing to be attained.

body.text: yasya kasyacidatiśayasya tatra kathañcidasata utpattau so 'tiśayastatra asan kathaṃ jāyeta? jāto vā sarvaḥ sarvasmājjāyeta iti tulyaḥ paryanuyogaḥ /
body.translated_text: If some special property (<s>atiśaya</s>) were in some way non-existent there and [yet] originated, how could that special property, being non-existent there, come into being? Or if everything came from everything, the objection would be equally [applicable].

body.text: nātiśayastatra sarvathā nāsti, kathañcitsata eva bhāvāditi cet / yathā nāsti sa prakāraḥ, tatra asan kathaṃ jāyeta?
body.translated_text: If [one says:] 'The special property is not absolutely non-existent there, but comes into being because it exists in some manner' — [we reply:] in the manner in which it does not exist, being non-existent in that manner, how could it come into being?

body.text: 28. na ca sarvathā sataḥ kaścijjanmārtha ityuktam / asato 'pi kāryasya kāraṇādutpāde yo yajjananasvabhāvastata eava tasya janma, nānyasmāditi niyamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 28. And it has not been said that there is any purpose in the origination of something absolutely existent. Even when an effect that was [previously] non-existent originates from a cause, whatever has the nature of producing a given [effect] — from that alone arises its production, not from another — this is the restriction.

body.text: tasyāpi sa svabhāvaniyamaḥ svahetorityanādisvabhāvaniyamaḥ /
body.translated_text: And that restriction of its nature is [itself restricted] by its own cause — thus it is a beginningless restriction of nature.

body.text: api ca - yadi mṛtpiṇḍe ghaṭo 'sti, kathaṃ tadavasthāyāṃ na paścādvadupalabdhiḥ, tadarthakriyā vā?
body.translated_text: Moreover — if a pot exists in a lump of clay, how is it that in that state [of the clay] there is no subsequent perception of it, or activity serving its purpose?

body.text: vyakteraprādurbhāvāditi cet / tasyā eva tadarthakriyādibhāve ghatvāt tadrūpasya ca prāgasattvāt kathaṃ ghaṭo 'sti? na hi rūpāntarasya sattve rūpāntaramasti /
body.translated_text: If [one says:] 'Because the manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) has not yet appeared' — [we reply:] since it is precisely that [manifestation] which, when present, constitutes the pot's functional capacity, and since that form was previously non-existent, how does the pot exist [in the clay]? For when a different form exists, another form does not [thereby] exist.

body.text: na ca rūpapratibhāsavede vastvabhedo yuktaḥ, atiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: And it is not correct [to maintain] identity of the object when there is a difference in the appearance of form, because of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).

body.text: 29. tasmād yaḥ upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasvabhāvānupalabdhiḥ sa nāstyeva / na hi tasyatatsvabhāvasthitāvanupalabdhitaḥ, asthitiścātattvam, parasparaṃtathāsthitayoreva [tathāsthitayoriva?] sukhaduḥkhayoriti vyāptiḥ, asadvyavahāraniścayena anupalabdhiviśeṣasya / tenānupalabdhyā kasyacid vyavacchedaṃ prasādhayatā tasya yathoktopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptirūpatā darśanīyā /
body.translated_text: 29. Therefore, that which, though having a nature fit for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), is not apprehended — that simply does not exist. For its non-apprehension does not occur while it abides in its own nature; and non-abiding is non-reality (<s>atattvam</s>). The invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) between two things so situated — like pleasure and pain for those mutually so situated — is [established] through the ascertainment of the convention of non-existence by means of a specific non-apprehension. Therefore, one who seeks to establish the exclusion of something through non-apprehension must demonstrate that it has the character of being fit for apprehension as described.

body.text: upadarśyānupalabdhinirdeśāsamarthanaṃ svabhāvānupalabdhau, vyāpakānupalabdhāvapi dharmayorvyāpyavyāpakabhāvaṃ prasādhya vyāpakasya nivṛttiprasādhanaṃ samarthanam /
body.translated_text: Having shown [this], the justification of the statement of non-apprehension is, in the case of non-apprehension of the essential nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>): establishing the pervaded-pervader relationship (<s>vyāpyavyāpakabhāva</s>) between the two properties, and then demonstrating the absence of the pervader.

body.text: kāraṇānupalabdhāvapi kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ prasādhya kāraṇasya nivṛtti prasādhanaṃ samarthanam /
body.translated_text: In the case of non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇānupalabdhi</s>) as well: establishing the cause-effect relationship and then demonstrating the absence of the cause.

body.text: tadviruddhopalabdhiṣvapi dvayorviruddhayorekasya viruddhasyopararśanaṃ samarthanam /
body.translated_text: In the case of apprehension of what is contradictory (<s>viruddhopalabdhi</s>) as well: showing that among two contradictory [things], one contradictory [thing is present] — this is the justification.

body.text: evamanupalabdhau sādhanāṅgasyāsamarthanaṃ sādhanāṅgāvacanam / tad vādino nigrahasthānasamarthane [? nigrahasthānam, asamarthane] tasmin vyāpyāsiddheḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, in non-apprehension, the failure to justify a member of the proof (<s>sādhanāṅga</s>) constitutes failure to state a proof-member. That is a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) for the proponent, since there is a failure of the concomitant (<s>vyāpya</s>) in [establishing] that.

body.text: 30. athavā - sādhyate yena pareṣāmapratīto 'rtha iti sādhanaṃ, trirūpahetu- vacanasamudāyaḥ / tasyāṅgaṃ pakṣadharmādivacanam / tasyaika- syāpyavacanamasādhanāṅga- vacanaṃ, tadapi vādino nigrahasthānam / tadavacane heturūpasyaivāvacanam, avacane siddherabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: 30. Alternatively — a proof (<s>sādhana</s>) is that by which an idea not accepted by the opponents is established; it is the aggregate of statements of the triple-characterized reason (<s>trirūpahetu</s>). Its member is the statement of the property-of-the-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) etc. The failure to state even one of these is failure to state a proof-member, and that too is a point of defeat for the proponent, since in the absence of statement, there is no establishment.

body.text: 31. [pratijñādīnāmasādhanāṅgatvam]
body.translated_text: 31. [The non-proof-member character of thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) and the rest.]

body.text: athavā - tasyaiva sādhanasya yannāṅgaṃ pratijñopanayanigamanādi tasyāsādhanāṅgasya sādhanavākye upādānaṃ vādino nigrahasthānaṃ, vyarthāmidhānāt /
body.translated_text: Alternatively — whatever is not a member of that proof — such as the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), the application (<s>upanaya</s>), the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>), etc. — the inclusion of such a non-proof-member in the proof-statement is a point of defeat for the proponent, because it states something purposeless.

body.text: anvayavyatirekavacanayorvā sādharmyavati vaidharmyavati ca sādhanaprayoga ekasyaivābhidhānena siddherbhāvād dvitīyasyāsāmarthyamiti tasyāpyasādhanāṅgasyābhidhānaṃ nigrahasthānaṃ, vyarthābhidhānādeva /
body.translated_text: Or, since in a proof-application employing the method of agreement (<s>sādharmyavat</s>) or the method of difference (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>), the statement of either the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) or the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) alone suffices for establishment, the second is ineffective — and thus stating it too, being a non-proof-member, is a point of defeat, precisely because it states something purposeless.

body.text: nanu ca viṣayopadarśanāya pratijñāvacanamasādhanāṅgamapyupādeyameva / na, vaiyarthyāt / asatyapi pratijñāvacane yathoktāt sādhanavākyād bhavatyeveṣṭārthasiddhirityapārthakaṃ tasyopādānam /
body.translated_text: But surely the thesis-statement, even though a non-proof-member, should be employed to indicate the subject matter? No — because of purposelessness. Even without a thesis-statement, from the proof-statement as described, the desired conclusion is indeed established; therefore its inclusion is pointless.

body.text: yadi ca viṣayopadarśanamantareṇa pratīterutpattiḥ, kathaṃ na pratijñā sādhanādayaḥ [sadhanāvayavaḥ?]? na hi pakṣadharmavacanasyāpi pratītihetubhāvādanyaḥ sādhanārthaḥ, sa pratijñāvacane 'pi tulya iti kathaṃ na sādhanam?
body.translated_text: But if understanding arises without the indication of the subject matter, then why is the thesis not [itself counted among] the proof-members? For the statement of the property-of-the-subject too has no purpose as a proof other than being a cause of understanding — and that is equally true of the thesis-statement; so how is it not a proof[-member]?

body.text: kevalasyāsāmarthyādasādhanatvamiti cet / tattulyaṃ pakṣadharmavacanasyāpīti tadapi na sādhanāvayavaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If [one says:] 'It is not a proof because of its incapacity when alone' — the same applies equally to the statement of the property-of-the-subject, and so that too would not be a proof-member.

body.text: na hi pakṣadharmavacanāt kevalā [kevalāt?] pratipatterutpattiḥ /
body.translated_text: For understanding does not arise from the statement of the property-of-the-subject alone.

body.text: etena saṃśayotpattiḥ pratyuktā, pakṣadharmavacanādapi kevalādapradarśite sambandhe saṃśayotpatteḥ /
body.translated_text: By this, [the objection that] doubt arises [from the thesis-statement] is also answered, since doubt arises equally from the statement of the property-of-the-subject alone when the connection has not been shown.

body.text: tasmād vyarthameva sādhanavākye pratijñāvacanopādānaṃ vādino nigrasthānam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, the inclusion of a thesis-statement in the proof-statement is altogether purposeless and constitutes a point of defeat for the proponent.

body.text: 32. athavā sādhanasya siddheryannāṅgam - asiddhaḥ, viruddhaḥ anaikāntiko vā hetvābhāsaḥ tasyāpi vacanaṃ vādino nigrahasthānam, asamarthopādānāt /
body.translated_text: 32. Alternatively — that which is not a member of the proof's establishment — a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) that is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), or inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) — the statement of that too is a point of defeat for the proponent, because of employing something incapable.

body.text: tathā sādhyādivikalasya anvayāpradarśitānvayā tairapi [? ananvayāpradarśitānvayāderapi] dṛṣṭāntābhāsasya sādhanāṅgasya [?asādhanāṅgasya] vacanamapi vādino nigrahasthānam asamarthopādānādeva / na hi tairhetoḥ sambandhaḥ śakyate pradarśayitum / apradarśanādasāmarthyam /
body.translated_text: Likewise, a pseudo-example (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>) — one that is deficient in the property to be proved etc., or whose positive concomitance has not been demonstrated — the statement of such a [pseudo-]proof-member is also a point of defeat for the proponent, precisely because of employing something incapable. For the connection of the reason cannot be demonstrated through such [pseudo-examples]. From the failure to demonstrate, there is incapacity.

body.text: 33. athavā - siddhiḥ sādhanaṃ, tadaṅgaṃ dharmo yasyārthasya vivādāśrayasya vādaprastāvahetoḥ sa sādhanāṅgaḥ / tadvayatirekeṇāparasyāpyajijñāsitasya viśeṣasyāśāstrāśrayavyājādibhiḥ prakṣepo moṣaṇaṃ [ghoṣaṇaṃ?] ca paravyāmohanānubhāṣaṇaśaktivighātādihetoḥ, tadapyasādhanāṅgavacanaṃ vādino nigrahasthānam, aprastutābhidhānāt /
body.translated_text: 33. Alternatively — establishment (<s>siddhi</s>) is the proof; its member (<s>aṅga</s>) is the property of the subject matter that is the basis of dispute and the occasion for debate — that is the proof-member. The introduction or announcement of some other, uninquired-about, special [topic], beyond that [proof-member], by pretexts such as pseudo-scriptural authority etc., for the purpose of confusing the opponent, disrupting [his] power of response, etc. — that too constitutes a non-proof-member statement and is a point of defeat for the proponent, because of stating what is irrelevant.

body.text: ebhiḥ kathāviccheda eva; tathā viśeṣasahitasyārthasya prativādino 'jijñāsitatvāt / jijñāsāyāmadoṣḥ / jijñāsitaṃ punararthasyānyasya prasaṅgaparaṃparayā ye ṣa pannādinā (?) bahiḥ prativādinaḥ, prāśnikānāṃ ca nyāyadarśināmiti /
body.translated_text: By these [digressions], there is only interruption of the discussion; because the special [claim] together with [its details] is something the opponent has not sought to investigate. If there is inquiry, there is no fault. But what is inquired about, by the chain of incidental connections of another [unrelated] topic, leading the opponent astray through [such devices as] . . . — [this is faulty] for the audience and for those who discern correct reasoning.

body.text: ebhiḥ kathāviccheda eva karaṇīyaḥ / na hi kaścidarthaḥ kvacit kriyamāṇaprasaṅge na prayujyate, nairātmyavādinastu tatsādhane nṛtyagītyāderapi tatra prasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: By these [tactics], only interruption of the discussion should be effected. For there is no subject matter whatsoever that could not be connected when an incidental connection is being manufactured; but for the proponent of non-self (<s>nairātmyavādin</s>), in establishing that [doctrine], even dancing and singing could be connected to it incidentally.

body.text: yathā - pratijñābhidhānapūrvakaṃ kaścit kuryāt - 'nāstyātmā'; iti vayaṃ bauddhā brūmaḥ / ke bauddhāḥ? ye buddhasya bhagavataḥ śāsanamabhyupagatāḥ / ko buddho bhagavān? yasya śāsane bhadantāśvaghoṣaḥ pravrajitaḥ / ka ḥ punarbhadantāśvaghoṣaḥ? yasya rāṣṭrapālaṃ nāma nāṭakam / kīdṛśaṃ rāṣṭrapālaṃ nāma nāṭakam? iti prasaṅgaṃ kṛtvā 'nāndyante tataḥ praviśati sūtradhāraḥ'; iti paṭhet, nṛtyed, gāyecca / prativādī taṃ ca sarvaprasaṅgaṃ nānukartuṃ samartha iti parājitaḥ syāt / iti sabhyaḥ sādhusammatānāṃ viduṣāṃ tattvacintāprakāraḥ /
body.translated_text: For example — someone might, beginning with a thesis-statement, declare: 'The self does not exist'; we <s>Bauddhas</s> say this. Who are the <s>Bauddhas</s>? Those who have accepted the teaching of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>. Who is the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>? He in whose dispensation the Venerable <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s> went forth [as a monk]. And who is the Venerable <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>? He who [composed] the play called <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. What is the play called <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> like? — and having made this digression, he might recite: 'After the benediction, the stage manager enters' — and then recite, dance, and sing. And the opponent, being unable to reproduce all that digression, would be 'defeated.' Such would be the method of truth-inquiry of the learned, approved by the wise — [an absurd conclusion]!

body.text: 34. na caivaṃ prastutasya paryavasānaṃ sa bhavati [? sambhavati], 'aniścaya phalatvādanārambha eva vādasya /
body.translated_text: 34. And in this way, there is no completion of the topic at hand. 'Since the outcome is uncertain, there should be no commencement of debate at all.'

body.text: kathaṃ caiva jayaparājayau? prativādino 'pyananubhāṣaṇasyaivamprakārasya prasaṅgasya vistareṇānubhāṣaṇavyājena sambhavād, aniścitatvācca /
body.translated_text: And how then [could there be] victory and defeat? For the opponent too, by the pretext of an extensive response to such a digression, could avoid responding [to the actual issue] — and [the result] is uncertain.

body.text: tasmāt pratijñāvacanameva tāvanna nyāyyam / kutaḥ punastatrājijñāsitaviśeṣaprasaṅgopanyāsaḥ, tadvyākhyāprasaṅgavitathapralāpaśca?
body.translated_text: Therefore, even the thesis-statement itself is not legitimate [as a proof-member]. How much less then the introduction of irrelevant special [topics] in that context, and the false prattle of pretextual digressions in explaining them?

body.text: sarvaścāyaṃprakāro durmatibhiḥ śaṭhairnyāyasāmarthyenārthapratipādane 'samarthaiḥ pravartitaḥ /
body.translated_text: All such methods have been introduced by the dim-witted, the dishonest, those incapable of establishing a position by the power of logic.

body.text: yathā - 'puruṣātiśayapūrvakāṇi tanubhuvanakaraṇādīni'; iti pratijñāya tanukaraṇabhuvanavyākhyāvyājena sakalavaiśeṣikaśāstrārthaghoṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: For example — having declared the thesis 'Body, world, and their creation are preceded by a supreme person (<s>puruṣātiśaya</s>),' [one might,] under the pretext of explaining body, creation, and world, proclaim the entire content of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system.

body.text: 'nityaḥ śabdo 'nityo vā'; iti vāde dvādaśalakṣaṇaprapañcaprakāśanaśāstra praṇetṛ- jaiminipratijñātatattvanityatādhikaraṇaśabdaghaṭānyatarasadvitīyo ghaḥṭa iti pratijñāmuparacayya dvādaśalakṣaṇādivyākhyānam /
body.translated_text: In the debate 'Sound is eternal or non-eternal,' [one might,] having set up a thesis incorporating the twelve-feature elaboration treatise, <s>Jaimini</s>'s thesis, the section on the eternality of reality, 'Sound is the second to either a pot or [something else]' — and then expound the twelve-feature [system] and the rest.

body.text: sarvo 'yaṃ durmatīnāmasāmarthyapracchādanopāyaḥ, na tu satyairastyupetaḥ, tattvaparīkṣāyāṃ phalādipratisaraṇadaṇḍaprayogādīnāmayuktatvāt /
body.translated_text: All this is a device of the dim-witted for concealing [their] incapacity. It is not [a method] adopted by truthful [debaters], since in the examination of reality, the application of sticks, resort to fruits [bribery], and the like are inappropriate.

body.text: 35. bhavatyeva nāṭakādighoṣaṇe 'rthāntaragamanāt parājaya iti cet, anyasyāpyajijñāsitasya kiṃ na bhavati? na hi tasyāpi kācid vivakṣitasādhyadharmasiddhau nāntarīyakatā / yathā hetupratyayapāratantryalakṣaṇasaṃskāraduḥkhatādisiddhimantareṇa nānityatāsiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: 35. If [one says:] 'In the proclamation of a play and the like, defeat does indeed occur through going to another topic (<s>arthāntaragamana</s>)' — does it not equally occur for any other uninquired-about [topic]? For that [play] too has no necessary connection with the establishment of the property to be proved. Just as without establishing the impermanence of [things] characterized by dependence on causes and conditions, the compounded nature [of things], suffering, etc., the impermanence [of sound] is not established [either].

body.text: tathāvidhastu dharmaḥ pṛthaganukto 'pi sādhyadharme 'ntarbhāvāt pakṣīkṛta eveti na pṛthagasyopanyāsaḥ, vyākhyānaṃ vā / tasmādevaṃvidhasyāpi tadānīṃ prativādino jijñāsitasyārthasya pratijñāyāmanyatraivopanyāso vyākhyānaṃ vā arthāntaragamanānnigrahasthānameva /
body.translated_text: However, such a property, even when stated separately, is already subsumed under the <s>sādhya</s>-property (property to be proved) and is thus included in the thesis; therefore there is no separate statement of it — or [it is] merely an explanation. Hence, even for such a property of the respondent under investigation at that time, its statement or explanation in a place other than the thesis constitutes departure to another topic (<s>arthāntaragamana</s>), which is itself a ground for defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>).

body.text: tena jijñāsitadharmamātrameva sādhanāṅgaṃ vācyaṃ, na prasaṅga upakṣeptavyaḥ, tadupakṣepe 'tiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, only the property under investigation itself should be stated as a component of the proof; a <s>prasaṅga</s> (absurd consequence) should not be introduced, because introducing it would lead to overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).

body.text: evamasādhanāṅgavacanaṃ vādino nigrahasthānaṃ prativādinā tathābhāve pratipādite, anyathā dvayorekasyāpi na jayaparājayāviti /
body.translated_text: Thus, the statement of what is not a component of the proof is a ground for defeat of the proponent, provided the respondent has demonstrated it to be so; otherwise, there is neither victory nor defeat for either of the two.

body.text: 36. [adoṣodbhāvanaṃ nigrahasthānam]
body.translated_text: 36. [Non-raising of a fault is a ground for defeat]

body.text: adoṣodbhāvanaṃ prativādino nigrahasthānam / vādinā sādhane pratyukte 'bhyupagatottarapakṣo yatra viṣaye prativādī yadā na doṣamudbhāvayati, tadā parājito vaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Non-raising of a fault (<s>adoṣodbhāvana</s>) is a ground for defeat of the respondent. When the proponent's proof has been stated, with respect to the accepted counter-thesis, whenever the respondent does not raise a fault, then he is to be declared defeated.

body.text: sādhanadoṣāḥ punaḥ - nyūnatvam, asiddhiḥ, anaikāntikatā, vādinaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭasyārthasya viparyayasādhanam, aṣṭādaśa dṛṣṭāntābhāsāśca / teṣāmanudbhāvanamapratipādanaṃ prativādinaḥ parājayādhikaraṇam /
body.translated_text: The faults of a proof are: deficiency (<s>nyūnatva</s>), non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>), inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>), proof of the opposite of what the proponent wishes to establish, and the eighteen pseudo-examples (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>). Not raising these — not demonstrating them — is the ground for the respondent's defeat.

body.text: tat punaḥ sādhanasya nirdoṣatvāt, sadoṣatve 'pi prativādino 'jñānāt, pratipādanāsāmarthyād vā /
body.translated_text: That, moreover, [may be] because the proof is faultless, or because, even though faulty, the respondent does not know [the fault], or because of inability to demonstrate [it].

body.text: na hi duṣṭa sādhanābhidhāne 'pi vādinaḥ prativādino 'pratipādite doṣe parājayavyavasthāpanā yuktā, tayoreva parasparasāmarthyopaghātāpekṣayā jayaparājayavyavasthāpanāt /
body.translated_text: For even when the proponent states a faulty proof, it is not proper to establish the respondent's defeat when the respondent has not demonstrated the fault, since victory and defeat are established only with reference to the mutual undermining of each other's capability.

body.text: kevalaṃ hetvābhāsād bhūtapratipatterabhāvāda pratipādakasya jayo 'pi nāstyeva / na hi tattvacintāyāṃ kaścicchalavyavahāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Only [this much is true:] because of the absence of a true cognition from a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), the non-demonstrator also has no victory. For in the investigation of truth, there is no practice of sophistry (<s>chala</s>).

body.text: yadyevaṃ, kiṃnu parājayaḥ, tattvasiddhibhraṃśāt? na anirākaraṇāt / nirākaraṇaṃ hi tasyānyena parājayaḥ, na siddhyabhāvaḥ, pratiyogyapekṣaṇāt / siddhyabhāvasya sādhanābhāve 'satyapi pratiyogini bhāvāt / pratiyoginaśca tannirākaraṇe 'sāmarthyāt parājayasyānutpatteraparājayaḥ /
body.translated_text: If so, what then is defeat? Is it from the loss of establishing the truth? No — from non-refutation. For refutation of one by another is [that one's] defeat, not the mere absence of establishment, because [defeat] depends on a counter-party. For the absence of establishment may occur even without a counter-party when there is no proof. And since the counter-party's defeat does not arise from inability to refute, [he is] undefeated.

body.text: tasmādayamasamarthasādhanābhidhāyyapi pareṇa tathābhāve 'pratipādite 'parājito vaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, even one who states an ineffective proof, when the other has not demonstrated it to be so, is to be declared undefeated.

body.text: 37. [vāde chalavyavahāraniṣedhaḥ]
body.translated_text: 37. [Prohibition of sophistry in debate]

body.text: chalavyavahāro 'pi vijigīṣuṇaṃ vāda iti cet / na, durjanavipratipattyadhikāre satāṃ śāstrāpravṛtteḥ / na hi parānugrahapravṛttā mithyāpralāpārambhāt sotkarṣaparapaṃsanādīn [svotkarṣaparapaṃsanādīn?] asadvyavahārān upadiśanti / na ca paravipaṃsanena lābhasatkāraślokopārjanaṃ satāmācāraḥ /
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] 'Sophistry (<s>chalavyavahāra</s>) too [is acceptable] in a debate for the sake of victory' — No, because the treatises of the virtuous do not engage in matters pertaining to the disputes of the wicked. For those motivated by benefiting others do not teach dishonest practices such as self-praise and denigration of others, beginning with false prattle. Nor is earning profit, honor, and fame through denigrating others the conduct of the virtuous.

body.text: nāpi tathāpravṛttebhyaḥ svahastadānena prāṇināmupatāpanaṃ satsammatānāṃ śāstrakāra sabhāsadāṃ yuktam / na ca nyāyaśāstrāṇi sadbhirlābhādyupārjanāya praṇīyante /
body.translated_text: Nor is it proper for treatise-authors and assembly-members approved by the virtuous to torment beings by their own hand toward those who so engage. Nor are treatises on logic composed by the virtuous for the sake of earning profit and the like.

body.text: tasmānna yogavihitaḥ kaścid vijigīṣuvādo nāma / parānugrahapravṛttāstu santo vipratipannaṃ pratipādayanto nyāyamanusareyuḥ satsādhanābhidhānena, bhūtadoṣodbhāvanena vā /
body.translated_text: Therefore, there is no such thing as a debate for the sake of victory prescribed by [proper] method. Rather, the virtuous, motivated by benefiting others, while instructing the confused, should follow reason — by stating a genuine proof, or by raising a genuine fault.

body.text: sākṣipratyakṣaṃ tasyaivānuprabodhāya / tadeva nyāyānusaraṇaṃ satāṃ / vādaḥ - uktanyāye tattvārthī cet pratipadyeta, tadapratipattāvapyanyo na vipratipadyeteti /
body.translated_text: Witnessed by direct perception, [this is] for the awakening of that very [confused person]. This alone is following reason for the virtuous. Debate [means:] if one who seeks truth accepts the stated reasoning — and even if he does not, another will not be confused.

body.text: tattvarakṣaṇārthaṃ sadbhirupahartavyameva chalādi vijigīṣubhiriti cet / nakhacapeṭaśastraprahārādīpanādibhirapīti vaktavyam! tasmānna jyāyānayaṃ tattvarakṣaṇopāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: If [one says] 'Sophistry and the like must be employed by the virtuous for the sake of protecting truth, against those who seek victory' — then one should say the same about scratching, slapping, weapon-strikes, burning, and the like! Therefore, this is not the superior method of protecting truth.

body.text: sādhanaprakhyāpanaṃ satāṃ tattvarakṣaṇopāyaḥ, sādhanābhāsadūṣaṇaṃ ca / tadabhāve mithyāpralāpādatra paropatāpavidhāne 'pi tattvāpratiṣṭāpanāt / anyathāpi nyāyopavarṇane vidvatpratiṣṭhānāt /
