body.translated_text: The declaration of [genuine] proof is the virtuous one's method of protecting truth, and the refutation of pseudo-proofs. In its absence, even though harm may be inflicted on the other through false prattle, truth is not established thereby. Even when truth is stated in substance by refuting the opponent [through sophistry], truth cannot be effectively proclaimed — nor [can] the respondent [be blamed] in this case, since the misapprehension is substantive.

body.text: tasmāt parānugrahāya tattvakhyāpanaṃ vādino vijayaḥ, bhūtadoṣadarśanena mithyāpratipattinivartanaṃ prativādinaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, proclaiming the truth for the benefit of others is the victory of the proponent; the turning back of false apprehension through showing genuine faults is [the role] of the respondent.

body.text: 38. athavā - yo na doṣaḥ sādhanasya, tadbhāve 'pi vādinā tadasādhayitum [tadā sādhayitum?] iṣṭasyārthasya siddhervighātābhāvāt, tasyodbhāvanaṃ prativādino nigrahādhikaraṇaṃ, mithyottarābhidhānāt / yathā sādhyatayāniṣṭo 'pi vādino dharmaḥ śāstropagamāt sādhya iti tadviparyāsena na virodhodbhāvanam /
body.translated_text: 38. Alternatively — that which is not a fault of the proof, since even when it is present it does not obstruct the establishment of the object the proponent wishes to prove — raising that is the ground for the respondent's defeat, from stating a false objection. Just as a property not desired by the proponent as the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) is [still] the <s>sādhya</s> by scriptural convention, [hence] raising a contradiction from its opposite [is not valid].

body.text: 'nāstyātmā'; iti tava pratijñāpadayorvirodha iti pratijñādoṣodbhāvanaṃ, 'prayatnāntarīyakaḥ śabdo 'nityaḥ, prayatnāntarīyakatvād'; iti hetordharmaviśeṣatvāt pratijñārthaikadeśa ityasiddhodbhāvanaṃ, sarvāṇi sādharmyavaidharmyasamādīni jātyuttarāṇi ityevamāderdoṣasyodbhāvanamadoṣodbhāvanam / tasya vādinā doṣābhāsatve prakhyāpite prativādī parājito vaktavyaḥ, pūrvapakṣe sādhanasya nirdoṣatvāt /
body.translated_text: For example: 'There is no self' — [objecting] 'there is a contradiction between your [use of] "your" and the thesis' — this is raising a thesis-fault. 'Sound is impermanent, because it is produced by effort' — [objecting that] the reason, being a specific property, is 'a part of the thesis-meaning' — this is raising non-establishment. All <s>jāti</s>-replies (sophistical rejoinders) such as [arguments from] similarity and dissimilarity — raising such [pseudo-]faults is [what constitutes] 'raising of a non-fault.' When the proponent has proclaimed these to be pseudo-faults, the respondent is to be declared defeated, since in the former case the proof is faultless.

body.text: doṣavati punaḥ sādhane na dvayorekasyāpi jayaparājayau, tattvāprakhyāpanāt, adoṣodbhāvanaṃ ca / apratipakṣāyāṃ ca pakṣasiddhau kṛtāyāṃ jetā bhavati /
body.translated_text: However, when the proof is faulty, there is neither victory nor defeat for either of the two, since truth has not been proclaimed — and [this counts as] 'non-raising of a fault.' And when the thesis-establishment has been accomplished without opposition, [the proponent] is the victor.

body.text: tasmājjigīṣatā svapakṣaśca sthāpanīyaḥ, parapakṣaśca nirākartavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, one who seeks victory must establish one's own thesis and refute the opponent's thesis.

body.text: nirdoṣe sādhanābhidhāne 'pi vādinaḥ prativādinā doṣābhāsa udbhāvite dūṣaṇābhāvatvakhyāpane eva jayaparājayau, nānyathā, bhāvatastattvābhidhāne 'pi pratipakṣanirākaraṇena tattvasya prakhyāpanāsāmarthyāt, na prativādinno 'pyatra, bhāvato mithyāpratipatteriti /
body.translated_text: Even when the proponent states a faultless proof, if the respondent raises a pseudo-fault, victory and defeat [are determined] only by the proclamation that [the objection] is not a [genuine] fault — not otherwise. For even when truth is stated in substance, without refuting the opponent one lacks the power to proclaim the truth; nor [is there defeat for] the respondent in this case, since the misapprehension is substantive.

body.text: idaṃ nyāyyaṃ nigrahasthānalakṣaṇamuktamasmābhiḥ / nyāyamatakhaṇḍanam
body.translated_text: This is the proper definition of grounds for defeat stated by us. [Now follows the] Critique of the <s>Nyāya</s> School's Position:

body.text: 39. anyatu na yuktamiti neṣyate / yatredaṃ yathoktaṃ nigrahasthānalakṣaṇaṃ nāsti, tasya nigrahasthānatvamayuktamiti noktamasmābhiḥ /
body.translated_text: 39. What others [i.e., <s>Naiyāyikas</s>] [hold] is not proper — and hence is not accepted [by us]. Where this above-stated definition of a ground for defeat does not apply, it is improper to call it a ground for defeat — this is what we have said.

body.text: [1] 'pratidṛṣṭāntadharmābhyanujñā svadṛṣṭānte pratijñāhāniḥ nigrahasthānam'; [nyā.sū. 5.2..2] ityatra bhāṣyakāramataṃ dūṣayitvā vārtikakāro yaṃ sthitapakṣamāha, tatraivaṃ brūmaḥ - pratidṛṣṭāntasya yo dharmastaṃ yadā svadṛṣṭānte 'bhyanujānāti nigṛhīto veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [1] 'Acceptance of a property of the counter-example in one's own example constitutes abandonment of the thesis, which is a ground for defeat' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.2] — having refuted the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s (commentator's) view on this, the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> (sub-commentator) states his settled position. To that we say: when one accepts in one's own example the property belonging to the counter-example, one is to be known as defeated.

body.text: tatra dṛṣṭaścāsāvante ca vyavasthita iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ / svadṛṣṭāntaḥsvapakṣaḥ / pratidṛṣṭāntaḥ pratipakṣaḥ / pratipakṣasya dharmaṃ svapakṣe 'bhyanujānan parājitaḥ / yathā 'anityaḥ śabda aindriyakatvād'; iti bruvan pratipakṣavādini sāmānyena pratyavasthite āha - 'yadi sāmānyamaindriyakaṃ nityaṃ śabdo 'pyevamastu'; ityeṣā pratijñāhāniḥ, prākpratijñātasya śabdānityatvasya tyāgāditi /
body.translated_text: There, 'example' (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) means what is observed and finally established. 'One's own example' means one's own thesis. 'Counter-example' means the counter-thesis. One who accepts the property of the counter-thesis in one's own thesis is defeated. For example, when one states 'Sound is impermanent, because it is perceptible,' and the opponent responds with a general [objection], [the proponent] says: 'If the universal is perceptible and eternal, let sound also be so' — this constitutes abandonment of the thesis, because of the relinquishing of the previously asserted impermanence of sound.

body.text: 40. atropagatapratijñātyāgāt pratijñāhānau viśeṣapratiniyamaḥ kiṃkṛto 'nena prakāreṇa pratijñāṃ tyajataḥ pratijñāhāniriti /
body.translated_text: 40. Here, since accepted thesis-abandonment already constitutes thesis-abandonment, what is the reason for the restriction to this specific mode — [that] abandoning the thesis in this manner is thesis-abandonment?

body.text: sambhavati hyanenāpi prakāreṇa hetudoṣodbhāvanādinā pratipakṣasādhanābhidhānena ca svapakṣaparityāgaḥ, parapakṣopagamaśca /
body.translated_text: For abandonment of one's own thesis and acceptance of the other's thesis is possible also in this manner: by raising a fault in the reason, or by stating a counter-proof.

body.text: idameva ca pratijñāhāneḥ pradhānaṃ nimittam / evaṃ pratipāditena pratijñā hātavyā, hānau ca parājaya iti /
body.translated_text: And this alone is the principal cause of thesis-abandonment. Thus, when demonstrated [to be wrong], one's thesis must be abandoned; and in [such] abandonment, there is defeat.

body.text: 41. idaṃ punarasambhaddhameva - 'sāmānyaṃ nityamaindriyakam'; ityukte 'śabdo 'pyevamastu; iti kaḥ svasthātmāsvayamaindriyakatvādanityaḥ śabdo ghatavaditi bruvan sāmānyenopadarśanamātreṇa nityaṃ śabdaṃ pratipadyeta?
body.translated_text: 41. But this [example] is entirely incoherent — when it is said 'the universal is eternal and perceptible,' who, being of sound mind, would accept that sound is eternal merely from the illustration of the universal, when he himself says 'Sound is impermanent because it is perceptible, like a pot'?

body.text: sāmānyasyāpi nityasyaindriyakatve tasyānitye ghaṭe darśanāt saṃśayitaḥ syāt / jātyā pratipadyetāpīti cet / tathapi kiṃ sāmānyopadarśanena?
body.translated_text: Even if the universal is eternal and perceptible, one would be doubtful because of seeing it [i.e., perceptibility] in a non-eternal pot. If [one says] 'he accepts it through the universal type (<s>jāti</s>)' — even so, what [is accomplished] by the illustration of the universal?

body.text: evameva nityaḥ śabdaḥ iti vaktavyam, jaḍasya pratipattau vicārābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: One should simply say 'sound is eternal' — there being no need for reasoning to produce conviction in the dull-witted.

body.text: na ca nityasāmānyopadarśanena taddharmaṃ śabde pratipadyamānena pratipakṣadharmo 'bhyanujñāto bhavati / 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ'; iti ca vadato nityaśabda ityāñjasaḥ pratipakṣaḥ syāt, (

children.translated_text: not 'the universal is eternal.'

body.translated_text: And by accepting permanence of sound through the illustration of the eternal universal, one does not thereby accept the property of the counter-thesis. Moreover, for one who says 'sound is impermanent,' the direct counter-thesis would be 'sound is eternal,'

body.text: tasmādaindriyakatvasya nityānityapakṣavṛttervyabhicārādasādhanāṅgasyopādānānnigrahārhaḥ, na pratipakṣadharmānujñyānena prakāreṇa pratijñāhāneḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, since sense-perceptibility, occurring in both the permanent and impermanent positions, is deviant [as a reason], one who adduces it as a non-component of proof deserves censure — not [one who] by the manner of conceding the opponent's property [thereby incurs] abandonment of the thesis.

body.text: 42. [2] 'pratijñātārthapratiṣedhe dharmavikalpāt tadarthanirdeśaḥ pratijñāntaram /'; [nyā. sū. 5.2.3] pratijñāto 'rtho 'nityaḥ śabda aindriyakatvādityeva, tasya hetuvyabhicāropadarśanena pratiṣedhe kṛte dharmabhedavikalpāt sāmānyaghaṭayo sarvagatatvāsarvagatatvadharmavikalpena pratijñāntaraṃ karoti - yathā ghaṭo 'sarvagato 'nityaḥ evaṃ śabdo 'pyasarvagato 'nitya iti / etatpratijñāntaraṃ nāma nigrahasthānaṃ sādhanasāmarthye 'pyaparijñānāt / sa hi pūrvasyāḥ 'anityaḥ śabda'; iti pratijñāyāḥ sādhanāttadā yām 'asarvagataḥ śabda'; iti pratijñāmāha, taddarśanāya taddarthanirdeśa ityāha / tadarthaḥ pūrvoktasādhyasiddhyarthaḥ / uttarapratijñānirdeśastadarthanirdeśaḥ / na ca pratijñā pratijñāntarasādhane samarthā, iti nigrahasthānam
body.translated_text: 42. [2] 'When there is denial of the stated thesis-meaning, the specification of that meaning due to the differentiation of the property is a counter-thesis.' [Nyāya Sūtra 5.2.3] The stated thesis-meaning is 'sound is non-eternal, because of being sense-perceptible.'

body.text: 43. atrāpi naivaṃ bruvatā pratijñāntaraṃ pūrvapratijñāsādhanāyoktaṃ bhavati / kiṃ tarhi? viśeṣaṇam / aindriyakatvasya hetoḥ sāmānye vṛttyā vyabhicāra udbhāvite 'sarvagatatve satyaindriyakatvasyahetorviśeṣaṇopādāne vyābhicāraṃ pariharati, na punaḥ pratijñāntaramāha; asarvagatatvasya śabde siddhatvāt, pratijñāyāśca sādhyanirdeśalakṣaṇatvāt /
body.translated_text: 43. Even here, what is said in this manner does not amount to a counter-thesis stated for the purpose of proving the original thesis. What then? It is a qualification. Since the reason of sense-perceptibility is deviant due to its occurrence in the general [class], this specification is for the purpose of demonstrating the restriction of the reason.

body.text: yadapyuktaṃ - 'pūrva pratijñāsādhanāyottarāṃ pratijñāmāha'; iti, tadapyuktam / na hi pratijñā pratijñāsādhanāyocyamānā pratijñāntaraṃ bhavati / kiṃ tarhi? hetvāderanyatamaḥ sādhyasādhanāyopādānāt / sādhananirdeśaḥ sa syāt, na sādhyanirdeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: As for what was said — 'he states a subsequent thesis for the purpose of proving the prior thesis' — that too has been addressed. For a thesis stated for the purpose of proving [another] thesis does not become a counter-thesis. Rather, [it serves as] a qualification.

body.text: udāharaṇasādharmyādeśca hetulakṣaṇasyāsarvagatatve bhāvāt, pratijñālakṣṇasya cābhāvāt / hetutvamasarvagatatve prayuktaṃ na pratijñāntaram /
body.translated_text: And because the defining mark of a reason [applies here] due to the non-universality [established] from the similarity with the example, while the defining mark of a thesis is absent — what is employed in [showing] non-universality is a reason, not a counter-thesis.

body.text: 44. atyantāsambaddhaṃ cedaṃ - pratijñāṃ pratijñāsādhanāyāheti / yo hi prāk pratijñāmuktvā hetūdāharaṇādikaṃ vaktuṃ jānāti, sa kiñcidanukramaṃ [kañcidanukramaṃ?] sādhanasya jānātyeva hi / jānan kathamavikalāntaḥkaraṇaḥ pratijñāmeva pratijñāsādhanāyopādadīta?
body.translated_text: 44. This is entirely incoherent — that one states a thesis for the purpose of proving a thesis. For one who, having stated a thesis first, knows how to state reason, example, and so on, follows a certain order.

body.text: upādadatā cānena pratijñāmātreṇa siddhiriṣṭā bhavati / tataśca na prāgapi hetuṃ brūyāt /
body.translated_text: And if one who adopts [this view] wished for establishment by mere thesis alone, then he would not state a reason even previously.

body.text: evaṃprakārāṇāmasambaddhānāṃ parisaṃkhyātumaśakyatvāt lakṣaṇaniyamo 'pyasambadaddha eva - pratijñāntarābhidhāne pratijñāntaraṃ nāma nigrahasthānamiti / evamprakārāṇāmekameva lakṣaṇaṃ vācyaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: Since it is impossible to enumerate such incoherent [points], even the restriction by definition is itself incoherent — [the claim] that 'the statement of a counter-thesis is a point of defeat called counter-thesis.'

body.text: na caivaṃvidhaḥ kaścid vivādeṣu dṛṣṭapūrvo vyavahāro yena tadarthaṃ yatnaḥ kriyate / na ca bālapralāpānuddiśya śāstraṃ pravartate / pravṛttau ca kā niṣṭā, teṣāmaniṣṭhānāt?
body.translated_text: And no such convention has ever been observed in actual debates that would warrant effort toward that end. Nor does a treatise operate with reference to childish prattle. And were it to so operate, what would be the restriction?

body.text: 45. dṛśyate ca viduṣāmapi nātinirūpaṇādasiddhābhidhānamiti vyavahāradarśanāt tādṛśaṃ parājayādhikaraṇaṃ vyavasthāpyate / tasmādihāpi yadi nivṛttākaṃkṣe vādini paro 'naikāntikatāmudbhāvayed, asādhanāṅgasyānaikāntikasyābhidhānānnigrahasthānaṃ vādinaḥ /
body.translated_text: 45. It is observed that even among the learned, due to insufficient examination, there occurs the statement of what is unestablished — hence, on the basis of this observed convention, such a basis for defeat is established. Therefore, here too, if, when the expectation has been resolved —

body.text: evaṃ yadi prativādī satsāmānyamaindriyakaṃ nityaṃ ca pramāṇena pratipādayituṃ śaknuyāt anuddiśyāpramāṇakaṃ śāstropagamaṃ, pramāṇenaiṣāmarthānāmapratipādanena bhūtadoṣodbhāvanametat / na kaścitparājayaḥ, abhyupagamamātreṇa vastusiddherabhāvāt, prativādinā doṣasyāpratipāditatvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus, if the respondent were able to establish by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) that what exists in general is sense-perceptible and eternal — without relying on scripture unsupported by <s>pramāṇa</s> — then, since the non-establishment of these meanings by <s>pramāṇa</s> [would be shown] —

body.text: pramāṇairasamarthitasādhanābhidhānāt tu jetāpi na bhavatīti /
body.translated_text: However, from stating a proof unsupported by valid means of knowledge, one does not even become a victor.

body.text: anityākāṃkṣe [? anivṛttākāṃkṣe] punarvādini na kaścad doṣoḥ, viśeṣaṇābhidhānena hetoḥ samarthanopakramāt /
body.translated_text: But for a debater whose expectation has not been resolved [and who continues to argue], there is no fault — because he has commenced the strengthening of the reason by stating a qualification.

body.text: 46. [3.] "pratijñāhetvorvirodhaḥ pratijñāvirodhaḥ /" [nyā.sū.5 2. 4.] yathā 'guṇavyatiriktiṃ dravyam; iti pratijñā, 'rūpādibhyo 'rthāntarasyānupalabdheḥ iti hetuḥ, so 'yaṃ pratijñāhetvorvirodhaḥ / etenaiva pratijñāvirodho 'lapyuktaḥ, yatra pratijñā vacanena [svavacanena? virudhyate / yathā - śramaṇā garbhiṇī, nāstyātmeti vā /
body.translated_text: 46. [3] 'Contradiction between the thesis and the reason is thesis-contradiction.' [<s>Nyāya Sūtra</s> 5.2.4] For example: 'Substance is distinct from qualities' is the thesis, and 'because something different from form and the like is not perceived' is the reason —

body.text: hetuvirodho 'pi, yatra pratijñayā heturvirudhyate / yathā - 'sarvaṃ pṛthak, samūhe bhāvaśabdaprayogād'; iti /
body.translated_text: There is also reason-contradiction, where the reason contradicts the thesis. For example: 'Everything is distinct; because the word existence is used with reference to aggregates.'

body.text: etena pratijñayā dṛṣṭāntavirodho vyākhyātaḥ /
body.translated_text: By this, contradiction between the thesis and the example is also explained.

body.text: 47. hetośca dṛṣṭāntādibhirvirodhaḥ, pramāṇavirodhaśca pratijñāhetvorvaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 47. Contradiction of the reason with the example and other [components], and contradiction with <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) of the thesis and reason, must also be stated.

body.text: yaḥ parapakṣaṃ svasiddhena gotvādinā vyabhicārayati, tad viruddhamuttaraṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: One who shows deviation of the opponent's position through a property like cowness established in one's own [system] — that should be understood as a contradictory response.

body.text: svapakṣānapekṣaṃ ca / yaṃ ca svapakṣānapekṣaṃ hetuṃ prayuṅkte - 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ aindriyakatvād'; iti, tasya svasiddhasya gotvāderanityavirodhād viruddhaḥ / iti parapakṣeṣvasiddhena gotvādinānaikāntikacodanāviruddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: And [the reason must be] independent of one's own position. When one employs a reason independent of one's own position — 'sound is non-eternal, because of being sense-perceptible' — that [reason] is contradictory because of the contradiction of cowness and the like, which are established in one's own [system], with non-eternality.

body.text: ubhapakṣasampratipannastvanaikāntikaḥ / yadubhayapakṣaṃ [yadubhayapakṣa- ?] pratipannaṃ vastu tenānaikāntikacodanā iti /
body.translated_text: But what is accepted in both positions is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). The charge of inconclusiveness is [made] by means of an entity accepted in both positions.

body.text: 48. atrāpi pratijñārthaḥ, sādhanavākye prayogapratiṣedhāt / tadāśrayastatkṛto vā hetudṛśṭāntayorna virodha iti na pratijñāvirodho nāma kiñcinnigrahasthānam /
body.translated_text: 48. Here too, [what matters is] the thesis-meaning, since the use [of a thesis-statement] is prohibited in the proof-sentence. Since there is no contradiction of reason and example with [something] based on or produced by the thesis, thesis-contradiction is not any point of defeat whatsoever.

body.text: syādetat / asatyapi pratijñāprayoge gamyamāno 'pi pratijñāhetvorvirodho bhavati / yathā - rūpādibhyo 'rthāntarasyānupalabdhistad guṇavyatiriktam, nopalabhyate ca rūpādibhyo 'rthāntaraṃ dravyam / ityukte 'pi gamyata eva sādhyasādhanayorvirodhaḥ - kathaṃ tato 'rthāntarasyānupalabdhiḥ, tadvyatirekaśceti /
body.translated_text: One might say: even without the actual statement of a thesis, a contradiction between thesis and reason that is understood [implicitly] is possible. For example: 'because something different from form and the like is not perceived' — that [substance] is distinct from qualities — there is no perception [of such a thing].

body.text: satyaṃ, syādayaṃ virodhaḥ, yadi hetuḥ sādhyadharmaviparyayaṃ sādhayet / yadi hyupalabdhilakṣaṇavyāptatvena [hyupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatveva?] upagatasya sato (

children.translated_text: [Reference marker: Vn 77]

children.text: ) dravyarūpādipratibhāsavivekena svapratibhāsānupalabdhistasya tadvyatireke nāsti [tadvyatirekeṇāsti?] iti iṣṭavyatirekaviparyayasādhanād viruddho heturasmābhirukta eveti / bhavatyevedaṃ nigrahādhikaraṇaṃ, yadyevaṃvidhaḥ pratijñāhetoḥ [? pratijñāhetvoḥ] virodha iṣṭaḥ / atha punarasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptirlupyate, tadā na kaścit pratijñāhetoḥ [? pratijñāhetvoḥ] virodhaḥ, vyatiriktānāmapi bhāvānāṃ kutaścid viprakarṣiṇāṃ tadvyatirekeṇānupalabdhāvapi vyatirekasya bhāvāt /
children.translated_text: — the non-apprehension of its own appearance through the distinction of the appearances of substance, form, and the like — since there is [or is not] in its exclusion from that — is a contradictory reason because it proves the opposite of the desired negative concomitance.

body.translated_text: True, this would be a contradiction if the reason established the opposite of the property to be proved. For if something accepted as pervaded by the conditions of apprehension —

body.text: 49. yaduktaṃ - 'svavacanapratijñāyāḥ [? pratijñāyāḥ] svavacanavirodhe pratijñāvirodhaḥ'; iti tatredameva nigrahādhikaraṇam, asādhanāṅgabhūtāyāḥ pratijñāyāḥ sādhanavākye prayogaḥ, na virodhaḥ, tadadhikaraṇatvāt /
body.translated_text: 49. As for what was said — 'when there is contradiction between a thesis of one's own statement and one's own statement, that is thesis-contradiction' — therein this alone is the basis for defeat: the statement of a thesis that is not a component of proof.

body.text: yadi pratijñānapekṣoḥ virodhaḥ syāt, syāt parājayāśrayaḥ / pratijñādhikaraṇatve punastatprayogakṛta eva parājayaḥ, asya prastāvopasaṃhārāvasānatvād vyarthaṃ virodhodbhāvanam, parājitaparājayābhāvād bhasmīkṛtānalavat /
body.translated_text: If the contradiction were independent of the thesis, it could be a basis for defeat. But when the thesis is the basis, the defeat is produced only by the statement of that [thesis], since the debate is bounded by its introduction and conclusion.

body.text: ye tu kecid vicāraprasaṅgeṣu ekatra sādhye bahavo hetava ucyante, teṣa / vikalpena tatsādhyasādhanāya vṛtteḥ sāmarthyam, anyathā dvitīyasya vaiyarthyāt /
body.translated_text: When, in the course of investigation, many reasons are stated for a single property to be proved, they function alternatively with the capacity to prove that [property] — otherwise the second would be purposeless.

body.text: yadi hi tatrāpyekaprayogamantareṇāparasya prayogo na sambhavet, na tadā dvitīyasya kaścit sādhanārthaḥ, pratītapratipādanābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: For if, even therein, without the employment of one [reason], the employment of another were not possible, then the second would serve no proof-purpose, since there would be no cognition [produced by it independently] to convey.

body.text: tasmānna pratijñāyāḥ svavacanavirodho nāma kiñcinnigrahasthānam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, contradiction of a thesis with one's own statement is not any point of defeat whatsoever.

body.text: na ca 'nāstyātmā'; ityatra kaścit pratijñāvirodhaḥ nāstyātmaśabdārthasya bhāvopādānatvaniṣedhāt / sabdārthaniṣedhe hi virodhaḥ syāt / na ca svalakṣaṇaṃ śabdārtha iti /
body.translated_text: And in 'the self does not exist,' there is no contradiction of the thesis, because the meaning of the word 'self' is denied only with respect to the adoption of [its] real existence. For contradiction would arise if the referent of the word were denied. And the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is not the referent of a word.

body.text: 50. yaḥ punaḥ pratijñāyā bādhanāddhetuvirodha uktaḥ, yathā - 'sarvaṃ pṛthak samūhe bhāvaśabdaprayogāt'; iti / nātra pratijñāprayogaḥ, nāpi hetoḥ, yena virodhaḥ syāt / kiṃ tarhi? pratipāditārthopadarśanenopasaṃhāravacanametasmāt [... vacanametatsyāt?] /
body.translated_text: 50. As for what was called the contradiction of the reason through the refutation of the thesis, namely: 'Everything is separate in an aggregate, because of the use of the words "existent" and "thing"' — here there is no statement of a thesis, nor of a reason, by which there could be contradiction. What then? It is a concluding statement showing the already-demonstrated meaning, and therefore [it would be such a statement].

body.text: anyaireva hetubhiḥ śabdasyaikaviśeṣānabhidhānam, anekārthasāmānyābhidhānaṃ ca pratipādya sarvasya śabdārthasya nānārtharūpatayaikavastuviśeṣasvabhāvatābhāvamupadarśayan śabdārthamadhikṛtya sarvaṃ pṛthagiti brūyāt /
body.translated_text: Having demonstrated by other reasons that a word does not denote a single particular and that it denotes a general [meaning] applicable to many referents, one would say, with reference to the referent of the word, that 'everything is separate,' by showing that all referents of words, being of the nature of diverse meanings, lack the nature of a single particular thing.

body.text: etena tadvirodhaḥ pratyuktaḥ /
body.translated_text: By this, the contradiction of that [thesis with the reason] is answered.

body.text: 51. dṛṣṭāntopadarśanaṃ caitad - 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakānityatvād'; /
body.translated_text: 51. And this is a demonstration by example: 'Sound is impermanent, because of [the conjunction of] being produced and impermanence.'

body.text: yathā kvacid arthe vipratipattau prasiddhamanekārthasāmānye śabdaprayogamupadarśya pratipāditavipratipattisthānaḥ sāmānyenopasaṃharati - sarvaṃ pṛthagiti /
body.translated_text: Just as, when there is a disagreement about a certain object, one demonstrates the well-known use of a word with a general [meaning] applicable to many referents, and then, having exhibited the point of dispute already demonstrated, concludes generally: 'everything is separate.'

body.text: yadi dṛṣṭāntaprayogaḥ, kimṛjunaivatatprayogakrameṇa na prayuktaḥ, vipratipattiviṣayaśca kiṃ na darśita iti cet /
body.translated_text: If [this is] the deployment of an example, why was it not presented straightforwardly in the order of that deployment, and why was the subject of the disagreement not shown? — if so objected,

body.text: na, samāsanirdeśāt / evamapi prayogadarśanād, asādhanavākyatvācca /
body.translated_text: No, because of the concise formulation. Even so, because the deployment is shown, and because it is not a statement of a proof.

body.text: ata eva na pratijñayā hetorbādhanam / na caikameva kiñcinnāstīti bruvāṇaḥ kaścit tatsamuccayarūpamekaṃ ca samūhamicchati, yena virodhaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: For this very reason, there is no refutation of the reason by the thesis. And no one who says 'no single thing exists' thereby accepts an aggregate, which has the form of a collection of those [things], as one — by which there could be contradiction.

body.text: yo 'pi 'yugapat kaṅkena yogād'; ityādinā paramāṇorbhedamāha, na tasyāpyekaḥ samuccayarūpaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭaḥ / kiṃ tarhi? abhāva eva, ekānekapratiṣedhāt / ataḥ so 'pi na samūhastasyeṣṭo na tatra śabda iti na virodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Even he who states the division of the atom by [arguments] such as 'because of conjunction with a feather simultaneously' and so forth — even for him, it is not desired to establish one [entity] having the form of an aggregate. What then? Simply non-existence, through the negation of both unity and plurality. Therefore, for him too, no aggregate is accepted, no word [applies] there, and hence there is no contradiction.

body.text: 52. na viruddho 'yaṃ pūrvakāt pratijñāhetuvirodhāt bhidyate, yena pṛthagucyeta /
body.translated_text: 52. This contradictory [reason] is not different from the previous contradiction between thesis and reason, such that it should be stated separately.

body.text: tatra hetupratijñayorbādhanam, iha pritijñayā hetorityasti bheda iti cet / arthavirodhe hi hetupratijñayorbādhyabādhakabhāvaḥ syāt / 'sarvārthavirodho dviṣu'; iti yamapi (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vādanyāya</s> 83]

children.text: ) [yadapi?] parasparaṃ bbādhakam, ekārthasannidhāvaparārthāsambhavāt, tatra hetupratijñayoḥ sahapṛthagvā bādhodāharaṇayorna kaścidarthabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) is mutually contradictory, [as stated in] 'all real contradiction is between two,' — because in the proximity of one meaning the other cannot exist — therein, whether the refutation of thesis and reason is taken together or separately, there is no real difference in meaning in the examples.

body.translated_text: There, the reason refutes the thesis; here, the thesis [refutes] the reason — this is the difference, if so objected. But the relation of refuted and refuter between reason and thesis would [only] arise in the case of a real contradiction. Even that which (

body.text: 53. api cāyaṃ viruddho vā sati hetuprayoge vyadhikaraṇatvādasiddha ityasiddhatā hetornigrahasthānam / sa khalūcyamāna evātaddharmatayā pratīto vaktuḥ parājayamānayati / parājite tasmiṃstadarthavirodhacintayā na kiñcit /
body.translated_text: 53. Moreover, this contradictory [reason], if the reason is employed, is either unestablished due to being in a different locus — and the unestablishedness of the reason is a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>). For when stated, that [reason], being understood as not a property of that [subject], brings about the defeat of the speaker. Once he is defeated by that, there is no [further] concern with considering the contradiction of its meaning.

body.text: api ca - sarvatrāyaṃ pratijñāhetvorvirodhaḥ sambhavan dvayīṃ doṣajātimabhipatati viruddhatāmasiddhatāṃ ceti /
body.translated_text: Furthermore — this contradiction of thesis and reason, wherever it may arise, falls under two classes of faults: contradictoriness (<s>viruddhatā</s>) and unestablishedness (<s>asiddhatā</s>).

body.text: viruddhatā siddhe hetordharmiṇi bhāve sādhyadharmaviparyaya eva, bhāva pratijñāvirodhāt /
body.translated_text: Contradictoriness (<s>viruddhatā</s>) is precisely the opposite of the property to be proved, when the reason is established as existing in the subject — this is contradiction with the thesis.

body.text: asiddhatāpunardharrmiṇi pratijñātārthasiddhau, viruddhayoḥ svabhāvayoḥ ekatrāsambhavāt, na cānyathā virodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Unestablishedness (<s>asiddhatā</s>), on the other hand, [arises] when the meaning asserted in the thesis is established in the subject, because two contradictory natures cannot coexist in one [locus], and contradiction is not possible otherwise.

body.text: asiddhe dharmasvabhāve 'bhihitayorhetupratijñātārthayorvirodhād virodhasambhava iti cet /
body.translated_text: If it is said: contradiction is possible when the nature of the property is unestablished, because of the contradiction between the stated reason and the asserted meaning of the thesis —

body.text: apramāṇayoge tūbhayordharmiṇi saṃśayaḥ / tathā sati hetordharmiṇi bhāvasaṃśaye 'siddhataiva hetudoṣa ityasiddhaviruddhābhyāmanyo na pratijñayā virodho nāma parājayahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: But when there is no valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for either, there is doubt regarding both [their existence] in the subject. In that case, since there is doubt about the existence of the reason in the subject, unestablishedness alone is the fault of the reason. Therefore, other than the unestablished and the contradictory, no [fault] called 'contradiction with the thesis' is a cause of defeat.

body.text: asiddhaviruddhe ca hetvābhāsavacanādevokte iti na pṛthak pratijñāvirodho vaktavya iti /
body.translated_text: And the contradictory and the unestablished are already stated by the statement of pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>); therefore, contradiction with the thesis need not be stated separately.

body.text: 54. ubhayāśrayatvād virodhasya vivakṣāto 'nyataranirdeśa iti cet / syādetat / pratijñāhetvorvirodha iti pratijñāhetū āśrityobhayāśrayo bhavati / tatra yadā (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vādanyāya</s> 86]

children.text: ) pratijñāvirodho vivakṣitastadā pratijñāvirodha ityucyate, yadā pratijñāyā hetorvā virodhastadā viruddho heturiti / ataḥ pratijñāvirodhaḥ, hetuvirodho vā ityadoṣoḥ /
children.translated_text: ) contradiction with the thesis is intended, it is called 'contradiction with the thesis'; when the contradiction is of the thesis with the reason, or [the reason with the thesis], it is called 'contradictory reason.' Therefore, whether it is called contradiction with the thesis or contradiction of the reason — this is no fault.

body.translated_text: 54. If it is said: since the contradiction has both [thesis and reason] as its basis, the specification of one or the other is according to the speaker's intention — this might be so. The contradiction of thesis and reason, relying on both thesis and reason, has both as its basis. Therein, when (

body.text: tatra hetorudāharaṇam - nityaḥ śabdaḥ utpattidharmakatvāditi / pratijñāvirodhasya - nāstyātmeti / pratijñāhetvoḥ parasparaviruddhodāharaṇam - guṇavyatiriktamityādi / pratijñayā hetuvirodhodāharaṇam 'nāstyeko bhava'; ityādikam iti / na, sarvahetvapekṣasya virodhahetvābhāsānatikramāt, yathoktaṃ prāk /
body.translated_text: Therein, an example of [contradiction] of the reason: 'Sound is eternal, because it has the property of origination.' Of contradiction with the thesis: 'The self does not exist.' An example of mutual contradiction of thesis and reason: 'That which is different from qualities,' and so forth. An example of contradiction of the reason by the thesis: 'There is no single existence,' and the like. No — because when dependent on the entire reason, it does not go beyond the contradictory pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), as was stated before.

body.text: anapekṣe ca kevale svataḥ prativirodhe [pratijñāvirodhe?] vivakṣite pratijñāhetvorvirodha iti hetugrahaṇamasambaddham /
body.translated_text: And when a mere independent self-contradiction is intended, without dependence [on any reason], the inclusion of the word 'reason' in the expression 'contradiction of thesis and reason' is unconnected.

body.text: na cotpattidharmatvānnityamityatrāpi hetuvirodho yuktaḥ / pratijñayā hi hetorbādhane hetuvirodhaḥ, iha tu hetunā pratijñā bādhyate iti pratijñāvirodho yuktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is it correct [to call] 'Sound is eternal, because it has the property of origination' a contradiction of the reason. For contradiction of the reason [means] the refutation of the reason by the thesis; but here the thesis is refuted by the reason — therefore, contradiction with the thesis is the appropriate [designation].

body.text: ubhayāśraye 'pi virodhe bādhyamānavivakṣayā tadvirodhavyavasthāpanāt /
body.translated_text: Even when the contradiction has both [thesis and reason] as its basis, the determination of 'contradiction with that' is made according to which is being refuted.

body.text: 55. yadapyuktam - etena pratijñayā dṛṣṭāntavirodhādayo 'pi vaktavyā bhaṇḍālekhyanyāyeneti, tatrāpi pakṣīkṛtadharmaviparyavati dṛṣṭānte virodhaḥ syāt / viruddhe ca dṛṣṭānte yadi pakṣadharmasya vṛttirananyasādhāraṇā prasādhyate viruddhastadā hetvābhāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: 55. As for what was said — 'by this, contradiction of the thesis with the example, etc., should also be stated, according to the principle of inventory listing' — in that case too, contradiction would arise when the example is contrary to the property adopted in the thesis. And when the example is contradictory, if the occurrence of the property of the thesis [in it] is demonstrated as non-occurring-elsewhere, then the pseudo-reason is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).

body.text: sādhāraṇāyāmaprasādhite vā tadvṛttiniyame 'naikāntikaḥ / avṛttau vāsādhāraṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: If [the occurrence] is general, or if the restriction of its occurrence [in the example] is not demonstrated, [the reason is] inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). If there is non-occurrence [in the example], [it is] exclusive (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>).

body.text: viruddhadṛṣṭāntāvṛttau viparyayavṛttau ca na kaścid hetudoṣaḥ, dṛṣṭāntavirodhaśca pratijñāyā iti cet /
body.translated_text: If it is said: when [the reason] does not occur in the contradictory example and does occur in the contrary, there is no fault of the reason, and the contradiction of the example is with the thesis —

body.text: na, tadāpi saṃśayahetutvānativṛtteḥ / dṛṣṭāntavirodho hi pratijñāyāḥ sādharmye doṣo na vaidharmye, abhimatatvāt /
body.translated_text: No, because even then the character of being a cause of doubt is not transcended. For contradiction of the example with the thesis is a fault in the case of agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>), not in the case of difference (<s>vaidharmya</s>), since [difference] is accepted.

body.text: sādharmyadṛṣṭānte ca viparītadharmavati vastutaḥ sādhyāvyabhicāre 'pi hetornāvyabhicāradharmatā śakyā darśayitumiti nāpradarśitāvinābhāvasambandhāt hetorniścayaḥ / tanna pratijñayā dṛṣṭāntavirodho hetvābhāsānativartate /
body.translated_text: And in a concordant example (<s>sādharmya-dṛṣṭānta</s>) that possesses a contrary property, even though the reason may in fact not deviate from the property to be proved, its character of non-deviation cannot be demonstrated — and therefore, since the invariable relation (<s>avinābhāvasambandha</s>) has not been shown, there is no certainty regarding the reason. Therefore, contradiction of the example with the thesis does not go beyond the pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>).

body.text: 56. ubhayathāpi doṣo 'stviti cet / na / na hetudoṣasya prāk prasaṅgena parājitasya doṣāntarānpekṣaṇāt /
body.translated_text: 56. If it is said: let there be a fault in both ways — no. For one who has already been defeated by the earlier presentation of the fault of the reason need not be examined for yet another fault.

body.text: viśeṣeṇa sādhanāvayavānukramaniyamavādinaḥ / udāharaṇasādharnyaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ viruddhe dṛṣṭānte na sambhavatīti prākprayuktasya hetordoṣeṇa parājaya iti nottaradṛṣṭāntāpekṣayā virodhaścintāmarhati /
body.translated_text: Especially for those who maintain a fixed order in the members of the proof — since concordant illustration (<s>udāharaṇa-sādharmya</s>), which is the characteristic of the reason, is not possible in a contradictory example, defeat occurs through the fault of the previously stated reason, and so contradiction with respect to a later example does not deserve consideration.

body.text: hetorapi dṛṣṭāntavirodhe 'sādhāraṇatvaṃ viruddhatvaṃ vā, vaidharmye yadi vṛttiḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: Even in the case of contradiction of the reason with the example — it is either exclusiveness (<s>asādhāraṇatva</s>) or contradictoriness (<s>viruddhatva</s>), if there is occurrence in the dissimilar [cases].

body.text: pramāṇavirodhe tu hetoryathā - 'na dahano 'gniḥ saityāt'; ityādi hyasiddho hetvābhāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: And when the reason is contradicted by a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — as in 'Fire is not hot, because of coldness' and so forth — this is an unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>) pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>).

body.text: pratijñāyā pramāṇavirodhaḥ svavacanavirodhena vyākhyātaḥ iti sarve evaite sādhanavirodhe hetvābhāseṣvantarbhavantīti hetvābhāsavacanenaivoktāḥ /
body.translated_text: The contradiction of the thesis by a means of valid knowledge has been explained as self-contradiction (<s>svavacanavirodhena</s>). Thus, all of these, being contradictions with the proof, are subsumed under pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) and are already stated by the statement of pseudo-reasons.

body.text: 57. yattu viruddhamuttaraṃ parapakṣe svasiddhena gotvādinānaikāntikacodaneti, tadasambaddhameva / yadi hi svasiddhena gotvādinā parasya vyabhicārasiddhimākāṅkṣeta, tasya tatsvapakṣaviruddhaṃ nābhimatamiti virodho yujyeta / sa hi svayaṃ pratipanne gotve hetuvṛtteḥ saṃśayāno 'pratipattimātmanastathā khyāpayati /
body.translated_text: 57. As for [the objection] that a contradictory reply — charging inconclusiveness through one's own established [notion of] <s>gotva</s> (cowness) and the like against the opponent's thesis — this is entirely irrelevant. For if one were to seek the establishment of deviation [of the reason] through one's own established <s>gotva</s> and the like, since that is not accepted by the other party as contradicting his own thesis, the contradiction would be justified. For he, having doubt about the occurrence of the reason when <s>gotva</s> is accepted by himself, thus manifests his own non-comprehension.

body.text: sa ca hetuḥ satyasati gotve 'prasādhitasādhanasāmarthyaḥ saṃśaye hetutvādanaikāntika eva /
body.translated_text: And that reason, whether <s>gotva</s> exists or not, having its probative capacity unestablished, is simply inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because it is a cause of doubt.

body.text: prasādhite tu sāmarthye gotve 'vṛttyā hetau na saṃśaya eva, sarvasaṃśayaprakārāṇāṃ parihāreṇa samarthanāt /
body.translated_text: But when the probative capacity is established, there is no doubt at all regarding the reason's non-occurrence in <s>gotva</s>, because establishment involves the elimination of all possible modes of doubt.

body.text: etena svapakṣānapekṣahetuprayogasyānaikāntikatā vyākhyātā / so 'pi svābhimatanityagotvavṛttihetumanityatve bruvāṇo 'samarthatayāsādhanāṅgatayā saṃśayahetumevāheti /
body.translated_text: By this, the inconclusiveness of a reason deployed without reference to one's own thesis is explained. He too, stating a reason whose occurrence is in eternal <s>gotva</s> as accepted by himself while [arguing for] impermanence, states only a cause of doubt, because of incapacity, because of not being a member of the proof.

body.text: yatpunaruktam - ubhayapakṣasampratipannena vastunānaikāntikacodaneti, tatrāpyavaśyaṃ saṃśayahetutvamukhenaivānaikāntiko vaktavyaḥ / tadasamarthite 'nyatrāpi tulyamiti nobhayasiddhetarayoranaikāntikatvaviśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: As for what was further said — charging inconclusiveness through an entity accepted by both parties — there too, the inconclusiveness must be stated precisely through the avenue of being a cause of doubt. If that [probative capacity] is not established, the same [objection] applies equally elsewhere, and hence there is no distinction in inconclusiveness between what is established by both parties and what is established by one.

body.text: 58. yadapyuktaṃ - 'dṛṣṭāntābhāsā hetvābhāsapūrvakatvāt tadabhidhānenaivoktā iti na pṛthag nigrahasthāneṣūktāḥ'; iti tadapyavayavāntaravādino 'yuktam / yo 'vayavāntaraṃ dṛṣṭāntahetoḥ [dṛṣṭāntaṃ hetoḥ?] āha tasya na hetvābhāsoktyā dṛṣṭāntābhāsoktirvyāpyā, tadvacanena gamyamānsya tasmāt sādhanāntarābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: 58. As for the statement: 'Pseudo-examples (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>) are preceded by pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), and are therefore already stated by naming those; hence they are not listed separately among the points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthānas</s>)'—this is also improper for one who holds [the example to be] a separate member [of the proof]. For one who states that the example is [a member] separate from the reason, the statement of pseudo-reasons does not entail the statement of pseudo-examples, because what is conveyed by the former would then entail the absence of a separate means of proof.

body.text: dṛṣṭāntābhāsānāṃ hetvābhāse 'pyantarbhāvād dṛṣṭāntasyāpi hetāvantarbhāva iṣṭo bhavati / tathā ca na dṛṣṭāntaḥ pṛthaksādhanāvayavaḥ syād, apṛthagvṛtteḥ /
body.translated_text: If pseudo-examples are included within pseudo-reasons, then the example itself would be included within the reason. And thus the example would not be a separate member of the proof, since it does not function independently.

body.text: yo dṛṣṭāntasādhyo 'rthastasya hetāvantarbhāvāddhetunaiva sādhita iti na dṛṣṭāntasya pṛthak kiñcitsāmarthyam /
body.translated_text: The object to be proven by the example is included within the reason; hence it is proven by the reason alone. Therefore the example has no separate capacity.

body.text: api ca - na kiñcit pūrvapakṣavādino hetvābhāsāsaṃsparśe nyāyyaṃ nigrahasthānamastīti tatsambhandhīni sarvāṇyeva hetvābhāsatāvacanenaiva uktānīti na pṛthagvācyāni syuḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover—there is no proper point of defeat for the opponent that is not connected with a pseudo-reason; thus all [points of defeat] related to it would already be stated by naming the pseudo-reason, and need not be stated separately.

body.text: arthāntaragamanāderapi hetoraśāmarthye eva sambhavāt / na hi samarthe hetau sādhye ca siddhe 'rthāntaragamanaṃ kañcidārabhate, asamarthasya mithyāpravṛtteriti /
body.translated_text: Because even digression (<s>arthāntaragamana</s>) and the like occur only when the reason is incapable. For when the reason is capable and the thesis is established, no one resorts to digression; it is the false activity of one who is incapable.

body.text: 59. [4] "pakṣapratiṣedhe pratijñātārthāpanayanaṃ pratijñāsaṃnyāsaḥ /" [nyā. sū.5.2.5] yaṃ pratijñātamartham 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ eindriyakatvād'; iti sāmānyavṛttyā hetorvyabhicārapradarśanena saḥ pratiṣedhe kṛte, 'ka evamāha- anityaḥ śabdaḥ'; iti parityajati, tasya pratijñāsaṃnyāso nāma nigrahasthānamiti /
body.translated_text: 59. [4.] 'When the thesis is refuted, the abandonment of the proposed thesis is [the point of defeat called] abandonment of the proposition (<s>pratijñā-saṃnyāsa</s>).' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.5] When the proposed thesis—'Sound is impermanent, because it is produced by the senses'—is refuted by showing the deviation of the reason from the universal [relation], and the proponent says 'Who says sound is impermanent?' and abandons [his thesis], that is the point of defeat called abandonment of the proposition.

body.text: atrāpi yadyudbhāvite 'pi hetorvyabhicāre na sapakṣaṃ [svapakṣaṃ parityajati?[, kiṃ na gṛhyeta? anigṛha ta [?anigṛhīta] eva hetvābhāsābhidhānāditi cet /
body.translated_text: Here too: if, even when the deviation of the reason is exposed, [the proponent] does not abandon his thesis, what [then]? Would he not be defeated? He would be defeated already by the statement that the reason is a pseudo-reason.

body.text: kimidānīmuttarapratijñāsaṃnyāsāpekṣayā tasya tadevādyaṃ nigrahasthānamiti kimanyairaśaktaparicchedaiḥ klībapralāpapraceṣṭitairupanyastaiḥ? evaṃ hi atiprasaṅgaḥ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vādanyāya</s> 95]

children.text: ) syāt / pakṣapratiṣedhe tūṣṇīmbhavatastūṣṇīmbhāvo nāma nigrahasthānam, prapalāyamānasya prapalāyitaṃ nāmeti evamādyapi vācyaṃ syāt / tasmādetadapi asambaddhamiti /
children.translated_text: If, when the thesis is refuted, [the proponent] remains silent, there would be a point of defeat called 'silence'; if he flees, [there would be one called] 'flight'—and so forth. Therefore this too is incoherent.

body.translated_text: Now, if the primary point of defeat is the initial [pseudo-reason], in expectation of the subsequent abandonment of the proposition—what [is the point] of listing other [points of defeat], which are impotent discriminations and effeminate prattlings? For thus there would be over-extension—

body.text: 60. [5.] 'aviśeṣokte hetau pratiṣiddhe viśeṣamicchato hetvantaram / "[nya.sū.5.2.6.] nidarśanam - 'ekaprakṛtīdaṃ vyaktaṃ, parimāṇāt, mṛtpūrvakāṇāṃ śarāvaprabhṛtīnaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ parimāṇam'; iti /
body.translated_text: 60. [5.] 'When the reason stated without specification is refuted, and [the proponent] desires a specification, that is [the point of defeat called] another reason (<s>hetvantara</s>).' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.6] Illustration: 'This manifest [world] has a single source (<s>prakṛti</s>), because of its finitude; for things preceded by clay, such as dishes etc., are observed to be finite.'

body.text: asya vyabhicāreṇa pratyavasthānam - nānāprakṛtīnāmekaprakṛtīnāṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ parimāṇamiti /
body.translated_text: The counter-objection through deviation [is]: 'Things of many sources and things of one source are both observed to be finite.'

body.text: evaṃ pratyavasthita āha - ekaprakṛtisamanvayaprakārāṇāṃ pariṇāmadarśanāt [parimāṇadarśanāt?] sukhaḥduḥkhamohasamanvitaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vyaktaṃ parigṛhyate [parimitaṃ gṛhyate?] / tasya prakṛtyantararūpasamanvayābhāvo 'sati [? prakṛtyantararūpasamanvayābhāve sati] ekaprakṛtikatvamiti tadaviśeṣokte hetau pratiṣedhaṃ bruvato hetvantaraṃ bhavati / sati hetvantarabhāve pūrvasya hetorasādhakatvānnigrahasthānam /
body.translated_text: When thus countered, [the proponent] says: 'From the observation of the mode of connection with a single source, all this manifest [world] is apprehended as pervaded by pleasure, pain, and delusion. In the absence of connection with the form of another source, [the world] is of a single source.' Thus, when the refutation is directed at the unspecified reason, stating another reason [constitutes the point of defeat]. Since in the presence of another reason, the former reason is non-probative, [that is] the point of defeat.

body.text: atrāpi pūrvasyaiva hetoranaikāntikasyābhidhānānnigṛhīte hetvantaracintā kvopayujyate? yadi prāksādhanavādī hetumanaikāntikamuktvā dattottarāvasaraḥ tenaiva nigṛhyate / adattottarāvasaro hetvantarābhidhāne 'pi na nigrahamarhati, avirāmāt /
body.translated_text: Here too, since the proponent is already defeated by stating the initial inconclusive reason, where is the need for considering another reason? If the proponent, having stated an inconclusive reason and given an opportunity for reply, is defeated by that very [reason]—and if, without having given an opportunity for reply, even upon stating another reason, he does not deserve defeat because [the debate is] uninterrupted.

body.text: 61. [6.] "prakṛtādarthādapratibaddhārthamarthāntaram" [nyā.sū. 5.2.7.] yathoktalakṣaṇe pakṣapratipakṣaparigrahe hetutaḥ sādhyasiddhau prakṛtāyāṃ kuryāt- nityaḥ śabdo 'sparśatvāditi hetuḥ / hetuśca nāma hinoterdhātostuśabde pratyaye kṛdantaṃ padam / padaṃ ca nāmākhyhātopasarganipātā iti prastutya nāmādīni vyācaṣṭe / idamarthānantaraṃ nāma nigrahasthānam, abhyupagatārthāsaṅgatatvāditi /
body.translated_text: 61. [6.] 'That which is unconnected to the matter at hand, departing from the subject under discussion, is [the point of defeat called] digression (<s>arthāntara</s>).' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.7] In the context of the agreed thesis and counter-thesis, when the establishment of the thesis from the reason is underway, [the proponent] says: 'Sound is eternal because of its intangibility'—this is the reason. 'And reason (<s>hetu</s>) is a <s>kṛdanta</s> word from the root <s>hi</s> with the suffix <s>tu</s>. And a word is either a noun, verb, prefix, or particle'—thus he proceeds to explain nouns etc. This [is the point of defeat called] digression, because it is incoherent with the agreed subject.

body.text: nyāyyametannigrahasthānaṃ, pūrvottarapakṣavādinoḥ pratipādite doṣa prakṛtaṃ parityajyāsādhanāṅgavacanamadoṣodbhāvanaṃ ca / sādhanavādinā hyupanyastasādhanasya samarthane (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vādanyāya</s> 98]

children.text: ) kartavye tadakṛtvā parasya prasaṅgenāprasaṅgena vātannāntarīyakasyābhidhānamuttaravādino 'pi doṣodbhāvanamātrādaparasyopakṣepa iti /
children.translated_text: without doing that, either by the other's application or non-application, the statement of what is not entailed [by the proof]—and for the respondent too, merely exposing a fault and then introducing [another unrelated topic].

body.translated_text: This is a proper point of defeat: when, for the proponent or respondent, the fault having been demonstrated, [one] abandons the matter at hand and states what is not a member of the proof, and does not expose the fault. For the proponent, when the justification of the presented proof should be made—

body.text: 62. [7.] "varṇakramanirdeśavannirarthakam / "[nyā. sū.5.2.8] yathā 'nityaḥśabdo jabagaḍatvāt jhabhaghaḍhavad'; iti / sādhanānupādānāt nigṛhyate iti /
body.translated_text: 62. [7.] 'That which is meaningless (<s>nirarthaka</s>), like a recitation of the alphabet.' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.8] As: 'Sound is eternal, because of <s>jabagaḍa</s>-ness, like <s>jhabhaghaḍha</s>'—[the proponent] is defeated because no probative member is employed.

body.text: idamapyasambaddham / na hi varṇakramanirdeśasiddhāvānarthakyaṃ yadeva kiñcidasādhanāṅgasya vacanaṃ tadevānarthakaṃ; sādhyasiddhyupayogino 'bhidheyasyābhāvāt, niṣprayojanatvācveti / prakāraviśeṣopādānamasambaddham /
body.translated_text: This too is incoherent. It is not the case that meaninglessness is established only in the recitation of the alphabet; whatever statement is not a member of the proof is itself meaningless, because there is no referent useful for the establishment of the thesis, and because it is purposeless. The specification of a particular form is incoherent.

body.text: vaterupādānādadoṣa iti cet / syādetat varṇakramanirdeśavaditi vatiratropāttaḥ so 'nyadāpi [so 'nyadapi?] ananurūpaṃ gṛṇhāti ityadoṣaḥ iti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'There is no fault because of the inclusion of the suffix -<s>vat</s> [in the sūtra].' [Reply:] It may be that the suffix -<s>vat</s> is employed here [meaning 'like'], but it also applies to other unsuitable [cases]—so this is not a defect.

body.text: na / arthāntārādernigrahasthānasyāvacanaprasaṅgāt / evaṃ hi tā nirarthakā vācyā nirarthakenaivābhidhānāhitam [nirarthakenaivābhidhānāt?] /
body.translated_text: No—because there would be the consequence of not stating other points of defeat like digression etc. For thus they should be called 'meaningless,' since they are stated with a meaningless designation.

body.text: na sādhyasiddhau anarthakaṃ nirarthakaṃ, yasya naiva kaścidarthastannirarthakamiṣṭamiti cet /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'What is meaningless is what is not useful for the establishment of the thesis; what has absolutely no meaning at all is meant by <s>nirarthaka</s> (literally: meaningless).'

body.text:
yasya kasyacidavādino 'pi hi nirarthakābhidhāne kiṃ na nigrahaḥ? nigrahanimittāviśeṣāt /
na; tasyehāprastāvāditi cet /
body.translated_text: Then why is one who states something meaningless, even if not a debater, not defeated? Since there is no distinction in the ground for defeat. [Objection:] 'No; because it is irrelevant to the debate here.'

body.text: āyātamiha - yo nirarthakaṃ bravīti, tasya tenaiva nigraha iti / tattunyaṃ sarvasyāsādhanāṅgavādina iti / sa sarvo nirarthakābhidhāno 'pyanenaiva nigrahasthānena nigrahārhaḥ /
body.translated_text: It comes to this: 'One who speaks something meaningless is defeated by that very [fact].' But that is the same for everyone who speaks what is not a member of the proof. So everyone who speaks something meaningless is deserving of defeat by this very point of defeat.

body.text: na ca varṇakramanirdeśaḥ sarvatra nirarthakaḥ; kvacitprakaraṇe tasyāpyarthavattvāt / tasmādatraivāsyānarthakyāt nigrahasthānatvam / api cānyadidamucyate - 'varṇakramanirdeśo nigrahasthānam'; iti; kapolavāditakaṃkṣyaghaṭṭitakamityevamādīnāmapi vācyatvāt /
body.translated_text: And the recitation of the alphabet is not meaningless everywhere; for in certain contexts it too has meaning. Therefore its being a point of defeat [applies only] because of its meaninglessness in this context. Moreover, it is another thing to say 'the recitation of the alphabet is a point of defeat'—since things like 'cheek-beating,' 'bell-ringing,' etc. would also need to be stated [as points of defeat].

body.text: 63. [8.] "parṣatprativādibhyāṃ trirabhihitamapyavijñātārtham / "[nya. sū. 5.2.9] yadvākyaṃ parṣadā prativādinā ca trirabhihitaṃ na vijñāyate kliṣṭaśabdamapratīta - prayogamatidrutoccāritamityevamādinā kāraṇena tadavijñātārthamasāmarthyasaṃvaraṇāya prayuktaṃ nigrahasthānamiti /
body.translated_text: 63. [8.] 'That whose meaning is not understood, even when stated three times before the assembly and the opponent (<s>avijñātārtha</s>).' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.9] A statement that is not understood even when stated three times before the assembly and the opponent—due to garbled words, unfamiliar usage, or excessively rapid utterance—such a statement of unintelligible meaning, employed to conceal incapacity, is a point of defeat.

body.text: nedaṃ nirarthakād bhidyate; sapadiprakṛtārthasambaddhaṃ gamakamevakuryāt, nāsyāsāmarthyaṃ, na ca jāḍyāt parṣadādayo na pratipadyante iti na vidvānnigrahamarhati /
body.translated_text: This does not differ from 'meaningless'; for if [the speaker] were to make [his statement] intelligible and connected with the subject at hand, there would be no incapacity on his part. And if the assembly does not understand due to stupidity, the learned one does not deserve defeat.

body.text: parṣatpratibhāsaparikalpyārhavacanāt nigrahārha eveti cet / nyāyavādino jāḍyāduktamajānan kiṃ na prativādī nigṛhyate? jāḍyāt parṣadādeḥ avijñātapratipādanasāmarthya iti vijetā na syānna nigrahārhaḥ / asambaddhābhidhāne nirarthakameveti na pṛthak vivakṣitārthaṃ [vivakṣitam avijñātārthaṃ?] nāma nigrahasthānamiti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'He deserves defeat because the worthy statement is determined by what appears to the assembly.' [Reply:] If the debater, not understanding what was said because of the assembly's stupidity, is not defeated—then how is the opponent defeated? If the assembly is too stupid to recognize [the speaker's] capacity for demonstration, the victor would not be [properly determined], and [the opponent] does not deserve defeat. When what is stated is incoherent, it is simply meaningless—so the point of defeat called 'unintelligible meaning' is not separately intended.

body.text: 64. [9.] "paurvāparyāyogādapratibaddhārthamapārthakam /" [nyā. sū. 5.2.10] yatrānekasya padasya vākyasya vā paurvāparyeṇa yogo nāstītyasambaddhārthatā gṛhyate, tatsamudāyārthāpāyād apārthakaṃ daśadāḍimādivākyavat / idaṃ kila padānām asambaddhāt [asambandhāt?] asambaddhavarṇāt nirarthakāt pṛthaguktam /
body.translated_text: 64. [9.] 'That which, due to the impossibility of sequence, has disconnected meaning, is incoherent (<s>apārthaka</s>).' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.10] Where many words or sentences have no proper sequence, so that their disconnected meaning is grasped—because the combined meaning is lost, [it is] incoherent, like the sentence 'ten pomegranates' etc. This is said to be stated separately from the meaningless [statement] of disconnected letters, because of the disconnection of words [rather than letters].

body.text: nanvevamasambaddhavākyamapi pṛthag vācyam; nobhayasaṅgrahādapārthakaṃ yuktam; nirarthakasya saṃgrahaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: But in that case, the incoherent sentence should also be stated separately; it is not proper to subsume both under '<s>apārthaka</s>,' because of the consequence of subsuming the meaningless.

body.text: evaṃvidhācca viśeṣasamāśrayāt pṛthag nigrahasthānalakṣaṇapralapane 'tiprasaṅgo 'pyuktaḥ / na ca saṅgrahanirdeśe kañciddoṣaṃ paśyāmaḥ / prabhede vā guṇāntaramiti yatkiñcidetat /
body.translated_text: And from taking recourse to such distinctions, the over-extension of prattling about separate definitions of points of defeat has already been stated. And we see no fault in stating them under a general heading. Whether there is a separate category in the subdivision—this is of no consequence.

body.text: 65. [10] "avayavaviparyāsavacanamaprāptakālam /" [nyā.sū. 5.2.11] pratijñādīnāṃ yathālakṣaṇamarthavaśāt kramaḥ, tatrāvayavānāṃ viparyayeṇābhidhānaṃ nigrahasthānam /
body.translated_text: 65. [10] 'The statement of the members in reversed order is untimely.' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.11] The order of thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) and other [members] follows the logical requirement of their definitions. Therein, stating the members in reversed order is a point of defeat.

body.text: na; evamapi siddheriti cet / na; prayogāpetaśabdatulyatvāt / yathā- gaurityasya padasyārthe goṇīti prayujyamānaṃ padaṃ kakudādimantamarthaṃ pratipādayatīti na śabdārthākhyānaṃ vyartham / anena ca padena gośabdameva pratipadyate, gośabdat (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vādanyāya</s> 105]

children.text: ) kakudādimantamartham, tathā pratijñādyavayavaviparyayeṇānupūrvīṃ pratipadyate, ānupūrvyā cārthamiti / tathā hi pūrvaṃ karmopādīyate mṛtpiṇḍādikaṃ loke, tataḥ karaṇam iti /
children.translated_text: the meaning [of an animal] possessing a hump etc. Similarly, through the reversal of members like thesis etc., one grasps the [correct] sequence, and through the sequence, the meaning. For indeed, in ordinary life, first the material (<s>karma</s>) such as a lump of clay is taken up, then the instrument — thus [the order matters].

body.translated_text: No — [one may say:] because establishment occurs even thus. [We reply:] No — because it is equivalent to a word not in standard usage (<s>prayogāpetaśabda</s>). Just as the word '<s>goṇī</s>' employed in the meaning of the word '<s>gauḥ</s>' conveys the meaning of [an animal] possessing a hump etc. — therefore, the explanation of word-meanings is not purposeless. And through this [non-standard] word one understands the standard word '<s>go</s>,' and from '<s>go</s>'

body.text: 66. tadetadunmattakasyonmattakasaṃvarṇanamiva prayogāpetaśabdavadetaditi / yadi goṇīśabdāt kakudādimatyarthe pratītiśabdānvākhyānaprayatnena [? pratītiḥ, śabdānvākhyānaprayatne na] arthaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 66. This is like a madman's description of a madman — [this talk of] 'a word not in standard usage conveys the meaning.' If understanding arises from the word '<s>goṇī</s>' regarding the meaning of [an animal] with a hump, [then] in the effort of explaining the word, we see no [independent] meaning.

body.text: goṇīśabdasyārthapratipādane 'sāmarthyāt / satyaṃ dṛṣṭā, na tu sākṣādityuktam /
body.translated_text: Because of the incapacity of the word '<s>goṇī</s>' to convey meaning [directly]. True, [understanding] is observed, but it is not direct — this has been said.

body.text: nanu goṇīśabdādapi loke pratītirdṛṣṭā / satyaṃ dṛṣṭā, na tu sakṣādityuktam /
body.translated_text: But surely, understanding from the word '<s>goṇī</s>' is observed in the world! True, it is observed, but it is not direct — this has been said.

body.text: uktametanna punaryuktaṃ; strīśūdrāṇāmubhayapratīterabhāvāt / yaḥ khalu ubhayaṃ vetti, śabdamapaśabdaṃ ca, sa eva pratipadyate / yastu nakkaśabdaṃ mukkaśabdameva vā vetti, na nāsāśabdaṃ, sa kathamapaśabdācchabdaṃ pratipadetat, tato 'rthaṃ pratipadyeta?
body.translated_text: This has been stated and should not be repeated. Because for women and <s>śūdras</s>, there is no understanding of both [correct and incorrect forms]. Indeed, only one who knows both — the [correct] word and the incorrect word — understands [the meaning through the incorrect form]. But one who knows only the word '<s>nakka</s>' or '<s>mukka</s>' and not the word '<s>nāsā</s>' [nose] — how could he, from the incorrect word, understand the correct word, and from that, the meaning?

body.text: dṛṣṭā cānubhayavedino 'pi pratītiriti /
body.translated_text: And understanding is observed even for one who does not know both [forms] — [this is said].

body.text: na paramparayā pratītiḥ, arthe 'samarthasya śabdo 'pi pratītijananāsāmarthyācca /
body.translated_text: Not through a chain of [intermediate] understanding; and because a word that is incapable regarding the meaning also lacks the capacity to generate understanding.

body.text: na hyarthe 'pi vācakatvaṃ nāmānyadeva, anyatra tadviṣayapratītijananāt /
body.translated_text: For denotative power with respect to meaning is not something different [from generating understanding]; since it generates understanding of that object even elsewhere [i.e., in non-standard words].

body.text: apaśabdaścecchabde pratītiṃ janayed, artha eva kiṃ na janayati? na hyetasyārthāt kañcid bhedaṃ paśyāmaḥ, yena taṃ pariharet /
body.translated_text: If an incorrect word generates understanding of the [correct] word, why does it not generate [understanding] of the meaning directly? For we see no difference between this [indirect understanding] and [understanding from] the meaning itself, such that one would avoid it.

body.text: akṛtasamayasya śabde 'pyapratītijananācca /
body.translated_text: And because even for the [correct] word, no understanding is generated for one who has not learned the convention.

body.text: na hyayamapaśabdaḥ śabde 'pi svabhāvataḥ pratītiṃ janayati, adarśanāt samaya eva tu janayet / samayavaśāt pravartate /
body.translated_text: For this incorrect word does not inherently generate understanding even of the [correct] word — [this is] not observed. Rather, convention alone would generate [it]. It operates through the force of convention.

body.text: evaṃ hi pratipattiparamparāpariśramaḥ parihṛto bhavati /
body.translated_text: Thus the toil of a chain of successive understandings is avoided.

body.text: 67. viparyayadarśanācca / śabdādarthamapratipadyamānā apaśabdaireva jñānaṃ vyutpadyamānā loke dṛsyante iti vyarthaṃ śabdānuśāsanam /
body.translated_text: 67. And from observing the reverse: people in the world are seen learning knowledge through incorrect words alone, without understanding the meaning from [correct] words — therefore grammar (<s>śabdānuśāsana</s>) is purposeless.

body.text: na vyarthaṃ, saṃskṛtaśabdavyutpattyarthamiti cet / ko 'yaṃ śabdānāṃ saṃskāraḥ? na hyeṣāṃ prajñābāhuśrutyādikaṃ saṃskāraṃ pasyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: It is not purposeless — [it is] for the purpose of learning refined (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) words — if [one says this]. What is this 'refinement' (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of words? For we see no refinement in them such as wisdom, learning, and the like.

body.text: nāpyeṣāmekāntena śravyatā / nāpyarthapratyāyane kaścidatiśayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is their pleasantness to the ear absolute. Nor is there any special advantage in conveying meaning.

body.text: na dharmasādhanatā, mithyāvṛtticodanebhyaḥ saṃskṛtebhyo 'pyadharmotpatteḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is there [religious] merit-producing capacity, since demerit arises even from refined [words used in] injunctions with wrong conduct.

body.text: anyebhyo 'pi viparyayeṇa dharmotpatteḥ / śabddsya suprayogādeva svargamodanaghoṣaṇā vacanamātram / na caivaṃvidhānāgamānādriyante yuktijñāḥ /
body.translated_text: Conversely, merit arises from other [non-refined words] too. The proclamation that 'from the correct use of words alone, [one attains] heaven and joy' is mere words. And those who know reasoning do not rely on such scripture.

body.text: na ca dānādidharmasādhanacodanāśūnyakevalaśabdasuprayogāt nagapātam iti bruvāṇasya kasyacinmukhaṃ vakrī bhavati / tasmānna saṃskṛto nāma kaścicchabdaḥ /
body.translated_text: And no one's face becomes crooked at [hearing] someone declare that 'merely from the correct use of words alone, without injunctions producing merit through charity etc., [one attains] heaven.' Therefore, there is no such thing as a 'refined' word.

body.text: śiṣṭaprayogaḥ saṃskāra iti cet / ke śiṣṭāḥ? ye viditavedyādiguṇayuktāḥ / kaḥ punareṣāṃ guṇotkarṣānapekṣo 'līkanirbandho yatte 'mūneva śabdān prayuñjate nāparān? na cātra kaścicchabde 'parokṣaḥ sākṣī, yata idameva prayuñjate nāparān śiṣṭā iti niścinumaḥ /
body.translated_text: If [one says:] 'The usage of the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) constitutes refinement' — who are the learned? Those endowed with qualities such as knowing the <s>Vedas</s> etc. But what groundless insistence on the superiority of their qualities [explains] why they employ precisely these words and not others? And there is no direct witness here regarding the word, by whom we might ascertain that 'the learned use precisely this and not other [forms].'

body.text: nanvevaṃ [na tvevaṃ?] vayaṃ guṇātiśayamapasyantaḥ saṃskāraṃ keṣāñcicchabdānāmanumanyāmahe, tadanvākhyānaṃ [tadanvākhyāne?] yatnaṃ vā; guṇātiśayābhāvāt / vedarakṣādikaṃ cāprayojanameva atatsamayasthāyinaḥ / satyapi guṇātiśaye na karaṇīya evānvākhyāne yatnaḥ, tatsvabhāvasyānyato 'pi siddheḥ / prākṛtāpabhraṃśadramiḍāndhrādibhāṣāvat / na hi pratideśaṃ bhāṣāṇāṃ kiñcillakṣaṇamasti / atha ca sampradāyasāmyāllokastathaiva pratipadyate, tāsāṃ ca prayogabhraṃśaṃ, tathā saṃskṛtānāṃ śabdānāṃ pratītirbhaviṣyati / iti jaḍapratipattirevaiṣā, yā śabdānāṃ lakṣaṇe pravṛttiḥ /
body.translated_text: But we, not seeing any superiority of quality, [should] not approve of the 'refinement' of certain words, nor [expend] effort in explaining them — due to the absence of superior quality. And the preservation of the <s>Vedas</s> etc. is itself purposeless for those not established in that tradition. Even if there were a superiority of quality, no effort need be made in grammatical explanation, since the nature of that [language] is established from other [sources] too. Just like <s>Prākṛta</s>, <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>, <s>Dramiḍa</s>, <s>Āndhra</s>, and other languages. For there is no particular rule for languages in each region. And yet, through similarity of tradition, people understand them in just the same way; and [despite] departures in usage of those [languages], understanding of refined words will similarly [arise]. Thus this engagement in the rules of words is nothing but dull comprehension.

body.text: 68. avayavaviparyaye 'pi yadi teṣāṃ vacanānāṃ sambandhapratītiḥ, na viparyayaḥ nāpi arthāpratītiḥ; sāmarthyāt / na hyatra kaścit samayaḥ pratyāyānāviśeṣe 'pi evameva avayavāḥ prayoktavyā iti /
body.translated_text: 68. Even when the members are reversed, if the connection among those statements is understood, there is neither reversal nor failure of meaning-understanding — by capacity [of the statements]. For there is no convention here that 'the members must be employed in precisely this order' even when there is no difference in what is to be conveyed.

body.text: sa eva teṣāṃ kramo yathāvastitebhyo 'rthapratītirbhavati / iti na viparyayāt pratītiḥ, tata ānupūrvīpratipattyā pratītiriti cet / nāpratīyamānasambandhebhyaḥ ānupūrvīpratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: That very order of theirs is [just the one] from which, as they stand, understanding of the meaning arises. Therefore, understanding is not [impeded] by reversal — [and if one says:] 'from that, understanding of the sequence leads to understanding [of meaning]' — [we reply:] there is no understanding of the sequence from [statements] whose connection is not understood.

body.text: yeṣāṃ śabdānāṃ kaścit sambandho jāyate [jñāyate?] 'idamiha sambadhyate'; iti, teṣu viditasambandheṣu kaḥ kasya pūrvo 'paro vā kramaḥ, yo yathāvasthitānāṃ sambandhaḥ pratīyate / na hi vākyeṣu padānāṃ kramaniyamaḥ kaścit, yathā rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ, puruṣo rajña iti /
body.translated_text: For those words whose connection is known — 'this is connected here' — when the connection is known, what [difference does] the order of earlier and later [make], since the connection is understood from them as they stand? For there is no fixed order of words in sentences — just as [one may say] '<s>rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ</s>' or '<s>puruṣo rājñaḥ</s>' [the king's man / the man of the king].

body.text: yāvadbhiḥ padairarthaparisamāptistadekaṃ vākyaṃ, yathā- 'devadatta gāmānaya kṛṣṇām'; iti / atra padānāṃ yathākāmaṃ prayoge 'pi nārthapratītau viśeṣa iti kaścit kramābhiniveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: A sentence is that [group of words] by which the meaning is completed — for example: '<s>Devadatta</s>, bring the black cow.' Here, even when the words are employed in any order, there is no difference in the understanding of meaning — so there is no insistence on order.

body.text: pratipāditaṃ ca pratijñāvacanāntareṇāpi yathā pratītirbhaviṣyatīti / pratīyamānārthasya śabdasya prayoge 'tiprasaṅgaḥ / pariśiṣṭeṣu ca sambandhaṃ pradarśya dharmiṇi bhāvaḥ pradarśyeta, dharmiṇi bhāvaṃ pradarśya sambandhaḥ pradarśyeta iti na niyamaḥ kaścid; ubhayathāpi pratītyutpatteḥ ityuktam / apratīyamānasambandheṣu ca padeṣu na tebhya ānupūrvyā api pratīteriti nedamapārthakād bhidyate iti nāprāptakālaṃ pṛthag vācyaṃ syāditi /
body.translated_text: And it has been demonstrated that understanding will arise even without a thesis-statement. In the employment of a word whose meaning is [already] understood, there is over-extension. And among the remaining [members], one might show the connection and then demonstrate the property in the subject, or demonstrate the property in the subject and then show the connection — there is no fixed rule, since understanding arises in either way — this has been said. And from words whose connection is not understood, there is no understanding even from the sequence — so this [point about reversed order] does not differ from [the point about] purposelessness, and need not be stated as a separate [point of defeat called] 'untimely.'

body.text: 69. [11.] "hīnamanyatamenāpyavayavena nyūnam /" [nyā.sū. 5.2.12.] yasmin vākye pratijñādīnāmanyatamo 'vayavo na bhavati, tadvākyaṃ hīnaṃ; sādhanābhāve sādhyāsiddheḥ /
body.translated_text: 69. [11] 'A [proof] deficient by even one of the members is incomplete.' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.12] A statement in which any one member — thesis etc. — is absent is 'incomplete,' because without the proof, the thing to be proved is not established.

body.text: na pratijñānyūnaṃ hīnaṃ; tadabhāve pratītibhāvāditi pratipāditam /
body.translated_text: A [proof] lacking the thesis is not 'incomplete,' since in its absence, understanding still occurs — this has been demonstrated.

body.text: hīnameva tat; nyūnatāyāmapi nigrahādityaparaḥ /
body.translated_text: It is indeed incomplete — because there is defeat even for deficiency — [so says] another.

body.text: yaḥ pratīyamānārthamanarthakaṃ śabdaṃ prayuṅkte, sa nigrahamarhet, nārthopasaṃhitasyābhidhāteti asamīkṣitābhidānametat / ata eva pratijñāyā na sādhanāṅgabhāva iti /
body.translated_text: One who employs a purposeless word whose meaning is [already] understood deserves defeat, not one who fails to state something [already] conveyed by the meaning — this [objection] is made without examination. For precisely this reason, the thesis is not a proof-member.

body.text: 70. [12] "hetūdāharaṇādhikamadhikam /" [nyā.sū.5.2.13.] ekena kṛtakatvād itarasya ānarthakyamiti tadetanniyamābhyupagame veditavyam / yatraikasādhanavākyaprayogapūrvako vicārastatrādhikābhidhānamanarthakamiti nigrahasthānam /
body.translated_text: 70. [12] 'That which is excessive beyond the reason and example is superfluous.' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.13] Since when one [of the two — <s>anvaya</s> or <s>vyatireka</s>] is given, the other is purposeless — this should be understood as applying to the accepted rule. Where investigation is preceded by a single proof-statement application, the additional statement is purposeless and constitutes a point of defeat.

body.text: prapañcakathāyāṃ tu na kaścidoṣaḥ, niyamābhāvāditi /
body.translated_text: But in extended discussion there is no fault, since there is no [such] rule — [this is said].

body.text: 71. [13.] "śabdārthayoḥ punarvacanaṃ punaruktamanyatrānuvādāt /" [nyā.sū. 5.2.14] śabdapunaruktam - anityaḥ śabdo 'nityaḥ śabda iti / arthapunaruktam anityaḥ śabdo nirodhadharmako dhvāna iti /
body.translated_text: 71. [13] 'Repetition in word or meaning is tautology, except for recapitulation.' [<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.14] Verbal tautology: 'Sound is impermanent, sound is impermanent.' Semantic tautology: 'Sound is impermanent, subject to cessation, evanescent.'

body.text: atra na śabdapunaruktaṃ pṛthagvācyam: arthapunaruktavacanenaiva gatatvāt / na hyarthabhede śabdasāmye 'pi kaścid doṣaḥ / yathā-
body.translated_text: Here, verbal tautology need not be stated separately, since it is already covered by the statement on semantic tautology. For when the meanings differ, there is no fault even when the words are the same. For example —

body.text: hasati hasati svāminyuccai rudatyabhiroditi /
body.translated_text: He laughs, laughs, when the master [laughs] loudly; he weeps, weeps bitterly;

body.text: kṛtiparikaraṃ svedo 'ṅgāraṃ [svedodgāraṃ?] pūrdhāvati [pradhāvati?] dhāvati //
body.translated_text: sweating with exertion, he runs, runs about;

body.text: guṇasamuditaṃ doṣāpetaṃ praṇindati nindati /
body.translated_text: he praises what possesses virtues and is free from faults — he censures, censures;

body.text: dhanalavaparikrītaṃ yantraṃ pranṛtyati nṛtyati //
body.translated_text: bought for a pittance, the puppet dances, dances.

body.text: yathā vā- yadyasmin sati bhavati bhavati, na bhavati na bhavati tattasya kāryamitarat kāraṇamiti /
body.translated_text: Or for example — 'If, when this exists, that exists — it exists; if it does not exist, it does not exist — then that is the effect of this, and the other is the cause.'

body.text: 72. gamyamānārthaṃ punarvacanamapi punaruktam; niyatapradaprayoge sādhanavākye yathā pratijñāvacanamiti arthapunaruktenaiva gatārthatvānna pṛthagvācyam /
body.translated_text: 72. Re-stating what is [already] understood is also tautology; in a proof-statement with a fixed [number of] components, such as the thesis-statement [being superfluous] — since the point is already covered by semantic tautology, it need not be stated separately.

body.text: ayamapi niyatasādhanavākye eva doṣo vaktavyaḥ; na vistarakathāyām / vyācakṣāṇo hi kadācidasamyak śravaṇapratipattiśaṅkayā sākṣiprabhṛtīnāṃ punaḥ punarbrūyāditi na tatra kiñcicchalam /
body.translated_text: This too is a fault to be stated only in the fixed proof-statement, not in extended discourse. For when explaining, one might sometimes repeat [things] again and again out of concern that witnesses and others have not heard or understood correctly — and there is no sophistry in that.

body.text: nāviṣayatvāditi cet; nāyaṃ gururna śiṣya iti na yatnataḥ pratipādanīyaḥ, yena punaḥ punarucyate, iti punarvacane nigraha eveti cet / na; sākṣiṇāṃ yatnena pratipādyatvāt, tadpratipādane doṣābhidhānāt, pratipādyasya śiṣyatvāt, vijigīśuvādapratiṣedhatvāt, trirabhidhānavacanāt, punarvacanaprasaṅge samayaniyamābhāvācca /
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] 'Because it is not the subject-matter [of debate]' — [we reply:] He is neither a teacher nor a student who must be painstakingly instructed, such that [the argument] is repeated again and again — therefore, in repetition there is defeat. No — because witnesses must be painstakingly instructed; because stating a fault in their instruction [is wrong]; because the one to be instructed has the status of a student; because debate for victory is prohibited; because of the rule of thrice-stating; and because in the case of repetition there is no convention restricting [it].

body.text: 73. na cedamadhikād bhidyate iti na pṛthagvācyam / viniyatapradaprayoge hi sādhanavākye ādhikyadoṣa iti punarvacane 'pi gatārthasyādhikyameva padasyeti /
body.translated_text: 73. This [i.e., repetition] does not differ from [the fault of] superfluity, and hence need not be stated separately. For in a proof-statement with fixed components, superfluity is a fault; therefore in repetition too, it is merely the superfluity of a word whose meaning has already been conveyed.

body.text: prapañcakathāyām anirūpitai kārthasādhanādhikaraṇāyāṃ nānārthasādhanepsāyāṃ nānāsādhanepsāyāṃ vā śrotuḥ hetvādi bāhulyasya punarvacanasya doṣatvāt / pratītapratyayābhāvād hetvādibāhulyaṃ vacanabāhulyaṃ ca sādhanadoṣa iti /
body.translated_text: In extended discourse, where the ground of proof has not been determined, or where one desires to prove multiple meanings, or desires multiple proofs, the multiplicity of reasons and the like, [or] repetition, is a fault of the proof — because the conviction has not been produced.

body.text: ādhikyapunarvacanayostulyadoṣa iti saṃgrahavacanaṃ nyāyyam; doṣābhāvādeva guṇābhāvāt, evamprakārāṇāṃ bhedānāṃ vacane cātiprasaṅgādityuktam /
body.translated_text: Since the fault of superfluity and repetition is the same, a summarizing statement is proper — because there is no quality precisely because of the absence of fault, and because stating all such varieties would lead to overextension — as has been said.

body.text: paryāyaśabdakalpo hyaparo hetuḥ pratipādite viṣaye pravartamānaḥ '; pratipādyasya viśeṣābhāvāt /
